Drain briefly on a rack. Serve warm, taking care as the caramel filling is very hot.

stages.title: Prepare banana
steps: Peel bananas and cut each lengthwise into two pieces.
Mix brown sugar with cinnamon in a shallow dish.

stages.title: Wrap rolls
steps: Roll each banana piece in sugar mixture and place on a wrapper.
Fold sides inward and roll tightly, sealing the edge with water.

stages.title: Fry until golden
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and fry rolls in batches until the wrappers are golden, about 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Turn until wrappers are crisp and sugar inside caramelises.

stages.title: Drain and serve
steps: Drain briefly on a rack rather than stacking hot rolls.
Serve warm, taking care as the caramel filling is very hot.

batch_05.json::Swedish Meatballs with Cr.title: Swedish meatballs with cream sauce
quick_steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk and finely grate in the onion. Mix with the beef and pork mince, egg and allspice until just combined.
Roll the mixture into small, even balls.
Brown the meatballs in the butter in a large pan over medium heat, in batches, until golden all over. Turn them gently.
Pour in the stock and scrape up the browned bits. Add the cream, return the meatballs and simmer until cooked through.
Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Serve with mashed potatoes and lingonberry jam, if you like.

stages.title: Mix meatballs
steps: Soak breadcrumbs in milk and finely grate onion.
Mix with mince, egg and allspice just until combined.

stages.title: Shape and brown
steps: Roll into small even balls and brown in butter over medium heat until golden all over.
Turn gently and work in batches to avoid overcrowding.

stages.title: Simmer in sauce
steps: Pour stock into pan and scrape up browned bits.
Add cream, return meatballs and simmer until cooked through.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Taste sauce and season with salt and pepper.
Serve with mashed potatoes and lingonberry jam if available.

batch_05.json::Nepalese Aloo Tama Bamboo.title: Aloo tama bamboo shoot curry
quick_steps: Peel and cube the potatoes, rinse the bamboo shoots, dice the onion and tomatoes, and mince the garlic.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion until translucent.
Add the garlic, cumin and turmeric and cook briefly until fragrant.
Add the potatoes, bamboo shoots, tomatoes and water and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for about 25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the broth has lightly thickened.
Season with salt, adding a little water if too concentrated, and serve hot with rice and coriander if you like.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Peel and cube potatoes evenly and rinse bamboo shoots to moderate their sourness.
Dice onion and tomatoes and mince garlic.

stages.title: Cook aromatics
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and soften onion until translucent.
Add garlic, cumin and turmeric and stir briefly until fragrant.

stages.title: Simmer curry
steps: Add potatoes, bamboo shoots, tomatoes and water and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook until potatoes are tender and the broth is lightly thickened.

stages.title: Balance and serve
steps: Taste the curry and adjust salt, adding water if overly concentrated.
Serve hot with rice and fresh coriander if desired.

batch_06.json::Vietnamese Pho Ga.title: Phở gà
quick_steps: Char the halved onion and ginger in a dry pan over high heat until fragrant and lightly blackened. Rinse off loose burnt bits and add to a large pot with the star anise and cinnamon.
Add the chicken and water. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, skimming off foam, and cook about 45 minutes until the juices run clear.
Remove the chicken and steep the broth a few more minutes. Cool the chicken, then shred the meat and discard the bones.
Strain the broth and season gradually with the fish sauce and salt.
Cook or soak the rice noodles per the packet and divide into bowls. Top with chicken and hot broth, then add the spring onions, Thai basil and a squeeze of lime.

stages.title: Char the aromatics
steps: Char halved onion and ginger in a dry pan over high heat until fragrant and lightly blackened.
Rinse off loose burnt bits and place in a large pot with the star anise and cinnamon stick.

stages.title: Simmer the broth
steps: Add chicken and water and bring just to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, skimming foam.
Cook for about 45 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the juices run clear, then remove it and continue steeping the broth briefly.

stages.title: Shred and strain
steps: Cool chicken enough to handle, remove bones and shred the meat.
Strain broth and season gradually with fish sauce and salt.

stages.title: Assemble bowls
steps: Soak or cook rice noodles according to the packet and divide into bowls.
Top with chicken and hot broth, then add spring onions, Thai basil and lime.

batch_06.json::Thai Som Tam.title: Som tam
quick_steps: Shred the green papaya into thin strands. Cut the long beans into short lengths and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Lightly pound the garlic and chilli in a mortar until fragrant. Add the palm sugar, fish sauce and lime juice and mix until the sugar dissolves.
Add the beans and tomatoes and pound gently until their skins just crack.
Fold in the papaya, pressing gently between tosses until it softens slightly.
Add the roasted peanuts and toss to coat. Taste and adjust until sour, salty, sweet and spicy are balanced.

batch_06.json::Chinese Dan Dan Noodles.title: Dan dan noodles
quick_steps: Whisk the sesame paste, soy sauce, vinegar and chilli oil with a little warm water until smooth and pourable. Divide between four bowls.
Fry the pork mince in a pan over high heat for 5 minutes, breaking it into crumbles, until browned.
Add the garlic and Sichuan pepper and cook for 1 minute until fragrant and the pork is cooked through.
Boil the noodles until springy and tender. Reserve a little noodle water, then drain.
Add the noodles to the sauce bowls and top with the hot pork. Toss, loosening with noodle water, and finish with the spring onions.

stages.title: Mix the sauce
steps: Whisk sesame paste, soy sauce, vinegar and chilli oil with warm water.
Adjust until smooth and pourable, then divide between bowls.

stages.title: Brown the pork
steps: Fry pork mince in a hot pan over high heat for 5 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned.
Add garlic and Sichuan pepper and cook until fragrant and pork is fully cooked.

stages.title: Cook noodles
steps: Boil noodles according to their packet until springy and tender.
Reserve a little noodle water and drain well.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Add noodles to sauce bowls and spoon over hot pork.
Toss thoroughly, loosening with noodle water and topping with spring onions.

batch_06.json::Japanese Onigiri.title: Onigiri
quick_steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it with the water to packet directions. Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff gently.
Mix the drained tuna with the mayonnaise and soy sauce, keeping the filling thick so it doesn't leak.
Wet your hands and lightly salt your palms. Flatten a handful of warm rice, enclose a spoonful of filling and shape into a firm triangle.
Wrap each triangle in a strip of nori just before eating. Serve at room temperature.

batch_06.json::Spanish Patatas Bravas.title: Patatas bravas
quick_steps: Cut the potatoes into even cubes and simmer in salted water for about 10 minutes, until barely tender. Drain and steam-dry for several minutes.
Toss the potatoes with the olive oil and salt, then spread them on a preheated tray.
Roast at 220°C for about 35 minutes, turning once, until deeply golden and crunchy.
Meanwhile, in a pan over low heat, fry the garlic, smoked paprika and chilli flakes for a few seconds.
Add the passata, sherry vinegar and sugar and simmer for about 10 minutes, until thickened.
Season the hot potatoes with salt and transfer to a serving dish. Spoon the sauce over some, leaving the rest crisp.

batch_06.json::American Eggs Benedict.title: Eggs Benedict
quick_steps: Melt the butter and let it cool slightly. Whisk the egg yolks with the lemon juice over low heat for a few minutes.
Slowly whisk in the warm butter until thick and silky, keeping it below a simmer.
Split the English muffins and toast until golden at the edges.
Warm the ham in a dry skillet over medium heat until heated through, then arrange on the muffin halves.
Bring a wide pan of water to a bare simmer over medium heat and add the vinegar. Slide in the eggs from small cups and cook until the whites set and the yolks stay soft.
Lift the eggs out, blot off excess water and place on the ham. Spoon over the hollandaise and finish with the cayenne.

batch_06.json::Indian Chicken Biryani.title: Chicken biryani
quick_steps: Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala and turmeric for at least 30 minutes in the fridge.
Soak the rice briefly, then boil in salted water until about 70% cooked. Drain while the grains are still firm.
Fry the sliced onions on medium-high heat until deeply golden. Cook the marinated chicken until nearly cooked through.
Layer the chicken, rice, onions, mint and saffron steeped in the milk in a heavy pot.
Cover tightly and cook on very low heat until the chicken is cooked through and the rice is tender.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff gently.

stages.title: Marinate chicken
steps: Mix chicken with yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala and turmeric.
Refrigerate for at least thirty minutes while preparing rice and onions.

stages.title: Parboil rice
steps: Rinse and soak basmati rice briefly, then boil in salted water until about seventy percent cooked.
Drain promptly so grains remain firm enough to finish steaming.

stages.title: Layer the biryani
steps: Fry sliced onions on medium-high heat until deeply golden and cook marinated chicken until nearly cooked through.
Layer chicken, rice, onions, mint and saffron-infused milk in a heavy pot.

stages.title: Steam and rest
steps: Cover tightly and cook on very low heat until chicken is cooked through and rice tender.
Rest covered ten minutes, then fluff gently without crushing the grains.

batch_06.json::Middle Eastern Baba Ganou.title: Baba ganoush
quick_steps: Prick the aubergines and roast at 220°C for about 35 minutes, until the skins collapse and the flesh is very soft. For extra smokiness, char the skins over a gas flame first.
Cool the aubergines, scoop out the flesh and drain briefly in a sieve.
Mash the flesh with the tahini, lemon juice, grated garlic and cumin until creamy but still slightly textured.
Season with salt, adding more lemon if needed, then drizzle with olive oil and scatter over the parsley.
Serve with warm flatbread, if using.

stages.title: Char the aubergines
steps: Prick aubergines and roast at 220°C until skins collapse and flesh is very soft.
For a smokier flavour, char the skins over a gas flame first, turning until blackened all over.

stages.title: Drain the flesh
steps: Cool until manageable, then scoop out the soft flesh.
Drain in a sieve briefly to remove excess liquid and bitterness.

stages.title: Mix the dip
steps: Mash aubergine with tahini, lemon juice, grated garlic and cumin.
Stir until creamy but still slightly textured.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Taste for salt and lemon and drizzle with olive oil.
Scatter parsley on top and serve with warm flatbread.

batch_06.json::British Eton Mess.title: Eton mess
quick_steps: Hull and quarter the strawberries, then toss with the lemon juice and icing sugar. Leave for about 10 minutes until they release a light syrup.
Whip the chilled cream with the vanilla until soft peaks form. Stop before it turns stiff or grainy.
Crush the meringues into uneven chunks, keeping some large. Gently fold most of the berries and meringue into the cream.
Spoon into glasses and top with the reserved berries and meringue. Serve immediately while the meringue is still crunchy.

batch_06.json::Italian Cacio e Pepe.title: Cacio e pepe
quick_steps: Crush the peppercorns and toast in a wide dry pan over medium heat for about 1 minute, until fragrant. Add a ladle of hot pasta water.
Boil the spaghetti in lightly salted water until just shy of al dente, about 8 to 10 minutes. Reserve 2 cups of the cooking water, then drain.
Mix the Pecorino with a little warm (not boiling) pasta water into a thick, smooth paste.
Off the heat, toss the pasta in the pepper water, then stir in the cheese paste gradually.
Add small splashes of pasta water until glossy and creamy. Serve immediately.

stages.title: Toast the pepper
steps: Crush peppercorns coarsely and toast in a wide dry pan over medium heat for about 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add a ladle of hot pasta water to release their aroma.

stages.title: Cook pasta
steps: Boil spaghetti in lightly salted water until just shy of al dente.
Reserve at least two cups of starchy cooking water before draining.

stages.title: Make cheese paste
steps: Mix finely grated Pecorino with a little warm, not boiling, pasta water.
Stir until a thick smooth paste forms without clumping.

stages.title: Emulsify and serve
steps: Toss pasta in pepper water off the heat, then stir in cheese paste gradually.
Add small splashes of pasta water until glossy and creamy; serve immediately.

batch_06.json::Korean Japchae.title: Japchae
quick_steps: Boil the sweet potato noodles until tender and chewy. Drain, rinse briefly and toss with a little of the sesame oil.
Blanch the spinach, squeeze dry and season lightly.
Sauté the carrot, red pepper and mushrooms separately in a pan over medium heat until just tender, so each stays distinct.
Sear the beef strips in a hot pan over high heat until cooked through. Add the garlic, soy sauce and sugar and toss briefly.
Toss the noodles with the vegetables, beef and remaining sesame oil. Taste for soy and sweetness, then serve warm or at room temperature.

stages.title: Cook noodles
steps: Boil sweet potato noodles until tender and pleasantly chewy.
Drain, rinse briefly and toss with a little sesame oil.

stages.title: Prepare toppings
steps: Blanch spinach, squeeze dry and season lightly.
Sauté carrot, pepper and mushrooms separately over medium heat until just tender, so each stays distinct.

stages.title: Cook beef
steps: Sear thin beef strips in a hot pan over high heat until cooked through.
Add garlic, soy sauce and sugar and toss briefly.

stages.title: Combine and finish
steps: Toss noodles with vegetables, beef and remaining sesame oil.
Taste for soy and sweetness and serve warm or at room temperature.

batch_06.json::Italian Caprese Salad.title: Caprese salad
quick_steps: Slice the tomatoes into even rounds, arrange on a plate and season lightly with sea salt.
Drain the mozzarella, pat dry and slice into rounds as thick as the tomatoes.
Alternate the tomato and mozzarella slices, tucking whole basil leaves between them.
Drizzle with the extra virgin olive oil, add freshly ground black pepper and serve straight away at room temperature.

batch_06.json::Greek Loukoumades.title: Loukoumades
quick_steps: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and warm water into a thick, sticky batter. Cover and leave somewhere warm for about an hour, until bubbly and doubled.
Heat the frying oil in a deep pot over medium heat to about 175°C.
Drop small spoonfuls of batter into the oil in batches, using two oiled teaspoons. Fry, turning, until puffed and golden, then drain.
Warm the honey over low heat until pourable. Drizzle over the hot doughnuts and finish with the cinnamon and chopped walnuts.

batch_06.json::French Tarte Tatin.title: Tarte Tatin
quick_steps: Peel, core and quarter the apples, then toss with the lemon juice.
Melt the sugar in an ovenproof skillet over medium heat until amber. Swirl in the butter and a pinch of salt, then arrange the apples snugly in the caramel.
Cook the apples for about 5 minutes until they release some moisture, then take the pan off the heat.
Lay the puff pastry over the apples and tuck the edges inside the pan.
Bake at 190°C until the pastry is puffed and golden.
Rest for 5 minutes, then invert onto a large plate while the caramel is still fluid.

stages.title: Prepare apples
steps: Peel, core and quarter apples, keeping pieces similar in size.
Toss with lemon juice to prevent browning.

stages.title: Make caramel
steps: Melt sugar in an ovenproof skillet over medium heat until amber.
Swirl in butter and salt carefully and arrange apples snugly in the caramel.

stages.title: Cover with pastry
steps: Cook apples for about 5 minutes to release some moisture, then remove from heat.
Lay pastry over apples and tuck edges inside the pan.

stages.title: Bake and invert
steps: Bake at 190°C until pastry is puffed and golden.
Rest five minutes, then invert carefully onto a large plate while caramel is still fluid.

batch_06.json::Turkish Kisir.title: Kisir
quick_steps: Pour the boiling water over the fine bulgur in a bowl, cover tightly and leave about 15 minutes until tender. Fluff with a fork.
Stir the tomato paste and pepper paste through the warm bulgur until the grains turn reddish and fragrant.
Finely chop the spring onions, parsley and cucumber. Fold them into the cooled bulgur.
Add the pomegranate molasses, olive oil and lemon juice, then season with salt until tangy. Serve with lettuce leaves.

batch_06.json::Japanese Chicken Yakitori.title: Chicken yakitori
quick_steps: Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar over medium heat for about 10 minutes, until slightly syrupy. Set some aside clean for serving.
Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces and the spring onions into short lengths. Thread them alternately onto soaked bamboo skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning regularly, until golden and cooked through with no pink inside.
Brush with the glaze in the final few minutes until shiny, without burning.
Rest briefly, then brush with the reserved clean glaze and serve.

stages.title: Prepare the glaze
steps: Simmer soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar until slightly syrupy.
Set aside some clean sauce for serving and use the rest for basting.

stages.title: Thread the skewers
steps: Cut chicken into even bite-sized pieces and spring onions into short lengths.
Thread alternating pieces onto soaked bamboo skewers.

stages.title: Grill the chicken
steps: Grill over medium-high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning regularly so all sides cook evenly until golden and cooked through.
Brush with glaze during the final minutes to build a shiny coating without burning.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Check chicken is fully cooked through before removing from heat.
Rest briefly and brush with reserved clean glaze.

batch_06.json::Thai Coconut Rice.title: Coconut rice
quick_steps: Rinse the jasmine rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain well.
Combine the coconut milk, water, sugar and salt in a heavy saucepan, adding the pandan leaf if using.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Add the rice, cover tightly and cook on very low heat for about 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Don't lift the lid.
Remove from the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes, then discard the pandan and fluff with a fork.

stages.title: Rinse the rice
steps: Rinse jasmine rice gently until the water runs mostly clear.
Drain well so the liquid ratio stays accurate.

stages.title: Combine liquids
steps: Stir coconut milk, water, sugar and salt in a heavy saucepan.
Add pandan leaf if using and bring just to a gentle simmer over medium heat.

stages.title: Steam the rice
steps: Add rice, cover tightly and reduce heat to very low.
Cook without lifting the lid until liquid is absorbed and rice tender.

stages.title: Rest and fluff
steps: Remove from heat and leave covered for ten minutes.
Discard pandan and fluff gently with a fork before serving.

batch_06.json::Mexican Sopa de Lima.title: Sopa de lima
quick_steps: Simmer the chicken in the stock over low heat for about 20 minutes, until cooked through. Shred it and keep the broth warm.
Sauté the onion and garlic over medium heat until soft. Add the tomatoes and oregano, cook until the tomatoes break down, then stir into the broth.
Cut the tortillas into thin strips, toss with the oil and bake at 200°C until crisp and golden. Cool on a rack.
Return the chicken to the broth and warm through. Add the lime juice off the heat and serve with the tortilla strips.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Simmer chicken gently in stock over low heat until cooked through.
Remove and shred, keeping the broth warm.

stages.title: Build the soup
steps: Sauté chopped onion and garlic over medium heat until soft, then add diced tomatoes and oregano.
Cook until tomatoes begin to break down and stir into broth.

stages.title: Crisp tortilla strips
steps: Cut tortillas into thin strips and toss with oil.
Bake at 200°C until crisp and golden, then cool on a rack.

stages.title: Finish with lime
steps: Return shredded chicken to broth and warm through.
Add lime juice off the heat and serve with tortilla strips.

batch_06.json::Moroccan Zaalouk.title: Zaalouk
quick_steps: Prick the aubergines and roast at 220°C until collapsed and very soft, about 30 minutes.
Cool slightly, then scoop the flesh from the skins.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat with the garlic, cumin and paprika until fragrant.
Add the diced tomatoes and simmer until thick and jammy.
Mash in the aubergine flesh with a fork and cook uncovered until the excess moisture evaporates.
Add the lemon juice, chopped coriander and salt to taste. Serve warm or at room temperature with bread, if using.

batch_06.json::Mexican Tres Leches Cake.title: Tres leches cake
quick_steps: Whip the eggs and sugar until pale and voluminous, then fold in the flour, baking powder and vanilla.
Bake in a lined dish at 175°C until golden and springy, then cool slightly and prick all over with a skewer.
Whisk the evaporated, condensed and whole milk together, then pour slowly over the cake in several additions.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours, until the milk is fully absorbed.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and spread over the chilled cake. Slice and serve cold, with berries if you like.

stages.title: Bake the sponge
steps: Whip eggs and sugar until pale and voluminous, then fold in flour, baking powder and vanilla.
Bake in a lined dish at 175°C until golden and springy.

stages.title: Mix the milks
steps: Whisk evaporated milk, condensed milk and whole milk until combined.
Allow sponge to cool slightly, then prick all over with a skewer.

stages.title: Soak and chill
steps: Pour milk mixture slowly over the cake in several additions.
Refrigerate at least three hours until fully absorbed.

stages.title: Whip and finish
steps: Whip cream to soft peaks and spread over chilled cake.
Slice and serve cold, adding berries if desired.

batch_06.json::Portuguese Caldo Verde.title: Caldo verde
quick_steps: Soften the chopped onion with the salt in the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the potatoes, stock and water, and bring to the boil over high heat. Simmer on medium-low, partly covered, for 18–20 minutes until the potatoes fall apart.
Meanwhile, fry the sliced chorizo in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until browned and the fat has run out.
Blend the soup off the heat until completely smooth.
Return to medium heat, add the shredded kale and simmer for 4–5 minutes until tender and bright green.
Stir in the chorizo and its fat, season with pepper, and simmer for 1 minute until piping hot.

batch_06.json::Greek Avgolemono Soup.title: Avgolemono soup
quick_steps: Bring the stock to a gentle simmer in a large pot over medium heat. Add the rice and carrot and cook for about 20 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Reduce the heat to low, add the shredded chicken and warm through for about 5 minutes, without letting the soup boil.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice in a bowl until frothy. Slowly whisk in several ladles of hot broth to warm the eggs without scrambling them.
Take the pot off the heat and stir the egg mixture back in. Warm gently without boiling, then finish with the dill.

stages.title: Simmer rice
steps: Bring stock to a gentle simmer over medium heat and add rice and diced carrot.
Cook until rice is tender, then reduce heat to low.

stages.title: Warm chicken
steps: Add shredded cooked chicken and heat through gently.
Keep the soup below a rolling boil.

stages.title: Temper eggs
steps: Whisk eggs and lemon juice until frothy in a bowl.
Slowly whisk in several ladles of hot broth to warm the eggs without scrambling.

stages.title: Finish gently
steps: Stir tempered egg mixture back into soup off the heat.
Warm gently without boiling and finish with dill.

batch_06.json::British Welsh Rarebit.title: Welsh rarebit
quick_steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the ale until thick and smooth.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the grated cheddar, mustard and Worcestershire sauce. Once slightly cooled, mix in the egg yolk until smooth.
Toast the sourdough on both sides until pale golden, so it stays firm under the topping.
Spread the cheese mixture thickly to the edges of the toast.
Grill under a hot grill until puffed, golden and bubbling. Cool briefly before eating, as the cheese is very hot.

stages.title: Make the base
steps: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat and stir in flour for one minute.
Gradually whisk in ale to make a thick smooth sauce.

stages.title: Add cheese
steps: Remove from direct heat and stir in grated cheddar, mustard and Worcestershire sauce.
Mix in egg yolk once slightly cooled until smooth.

stages.title: Prepare toast
steps: Toast bread lightly on both sides until pale golden so it stays firm under the topping.
Spread cheese mixture thickly to the edges.

stages.title: Grill and serve
steps: Place under a hot grill until puffed, golden and bubbling.
Allow to cool briefly before eating as the cheese is very hot.

batch_06.json::Persian Shirazi Salad.title: Shirazi salad
quick_steps: Dice the cucumbers and tomatoes into 1 cm pieces, scooping the watery seeds from the tomatoes, and finely chop the red onion. Combine in a large bowl.
Toss the vegetables with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, until the onion softens. Tip off any pooled liquid.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil and dried mint, rubbing the mint between your fingers as you add it.
Pour the dressing over, toss to coat and season with black pepper and extra salt if needed. Serve straight away while crisp.

batch_06.json::Lebanese Chicken Shawarma.title: Lebanese chicken shawarma bowls
quick_steps: Mix the chicken with half the yoghurt, garlic, lemon, cumin, paprika and cinnamon. Refrigerate for 20 minutes while you prep the rest.
Rinse the rice and cook over low heat, covered, until fluffy, about 12 minutes.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes and season lightly with lemon.
Cook the chicken in a hot skillet or grill pan over high heat until charred in places and cooked through, about 15 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice across the grain.
Mix the remaining yoghurt with garlic and lemon for a sauce. Serve the chicken over rice with the salad and drizzle with sauce.

stages.title: Marinate chicken
steps: Mix chicken with half the yoghurt, garlic, lemon, cumin, paprika and cinnamon.
Rest refrigerated while rice and vegetables are prepared.

stages.title: Cook rice and salad
steps: Rinse basmati rice and cook, covered, over low heat until fluffy.
Dice cucumber and tomatoes and season lightly with lemon.

stages.title: Grill chicken
steps: Cook chicken in a hot skillet or grill pan until charred in places and fully cooked through.
Rest five minutes before slicing across the grain.

stages.title: Assemble bowls
steps: Mix remaining yoghurt with garlic and lemon for a quick sauce.
Serve chicken over rice with salad and drizzle with sauce.

batch_06.json::German Apple Pancake.title: German apple pancake
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) with a 25 cm ovenproof frying pan inside. Whisk the eggs, flour, milk and salt until smooth, then rest the batter.
Peel, core and slice the apples 5 mm thick. Toss them with the sugar and cinnamon until evenly coated.
Move the hot pan to the stovetop over medium heat. Melt the butter until foaming, about 30 seconds.
Add the apples and cook for 4–5 minutes, until just soft and the sugar turns syrupy.
Whisk the batter again and pour it over the apples. Bake for 15–18 minutes, until puffed, deep golden at the edges and set in the centre.
Serve straight away in wedges, before it sinks.

batch_06.json::Italian Gnocchi with Brow.title: Gnocchi with brown butter and sage
quick_steps: Grate the parmesan, zest the lemon and cut it into wedges. Dry the sage leaves and cut the butter into pieces.
Bring 3 litres of water to the boil over high heat and add the salt.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat until foaming. Cook the sage for 1–2 minutes, until crisp and the butter is nutty and golden brown. Lift the sage out onto paper towel.
Cook the gnocchi in the boiling water for 2–3 minutes, until they float. Scoop out 100 ml of cooking water, then lift the gnocchi out.
Return the pan to medium heat and toss the gnocchi with the reserved water for 1–2 minutes, until lightly golden and glossy.
Off the heat, stir through the zest, half the parmesan and pepper. Serve topped with the sage, remaining parmesan and lemon wedges.

batch_06.json::French Pear Belle Hélène.title: Poire Belle Hélène
quick_steps: Peel the pears, leaving the stems on, and trim the bases so they stand. Stir the water, sugar and vanilla in a medium saucepan over medium heat until the sugar dissolves, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the pears and reduce to low. Poach 15–20 minutes, turning, until a knife slides into the thickest part with no resistance.
Take the pan off the heat and cool the pears in the syrup for 20 minutes, then drain them stem side up.
Heat the cream in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until steaming with small bubbles at the edge. Pour over the chocolate, wait 1 minute, then stir until glossy.
Put a scoop of ice cream in each of 4 bowls, stand a pear beside it and spoon the warm sauce over.

stages.title: Make the poaching syrup
steps: Peel the pears, leaving the stems on, and slice a thin piece off each base so they stand upright.
Add 600 ml water, the white sugar and the vanilla extract to a medium saucepan just wide enough to hold the pears upright.
Stir over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until the sugar dissolves, then bring to a gentle simmer.

stages.title: Poach the pears
steps: Lower the pears into the syrup and reduce the heat to low so the surface barely bubbles.
Poach for 15–20 minutes, turning them occasionally, until a knife slides into the thickest part with no resistance.

stages.title: Cool the pears
steps: Leave the pears in the syrup for 20 minutes off the heat, turning once, until just warm or at room temperature.
Lift the pears out with a slotted spoon and drain them on a plate, stem side up.

stages.title: Make the chocolate sauce
steps: Put the chopped dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the thickened cream in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until steaming and small bubbles form at the edge, without boiling.
Pour the hot cream over the chocolate and leave for 1 minute, then stir until smooth and glossy.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Place a scoop of vanilla ice cream in each of 4 serving bowls.
Stand a drained pear beside or on top of each scoop.
Spoon the warm chocolate sauce over the pears and serve straight away.

batch_06.json::Jamaican Rice and Peas.title: Rice and peas
quick_steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs almost clear, then drain. Drain and rinse the kidney beans, and bruise the spring onions.
In a medium saucepan over medium heat, combine the coconut milk, water, spring onions, thyme, allspice and salt. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Stir in the kidney beans and simmer for 2 minutes, until heated through.
Add the rice and bring back to a simmer over medium heat. Cover tightly, reduce to very low and cook for 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Rest covered off the heat for 5 minutes. Discard the thyme stems and spring onions.
Fluff gently with a fork, season with a little more salt if needed, and serve hot.

batch_06.json::Mexican Arroz Rojo.title: Arroz rojo
quick_steps: Blend the tomatoes, half the onion and the garlic until smooth. Finely chop the remaining onion. Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain well.
Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan with a lid over medium heat. Cook the rice and chopped onion for 6–8 minutes, until pale golden and nutty.
Pour in the blended tomato and cook for 4–5 minutes, until thickened and the raw tomato smell fades. Add the salt.
Add the chicken stock and bring to the boil over medium-high heat. Scatter the peas on top, cover and reduce to low.
Cook for 15–18 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Rest covered off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and serve.

batch_06.json::Indian Besan Chilla.title: Besan chilla
quick_steps: Whisk the chickpea flour, salt and cumin with 260 ml water into a smooth, thick but pourable batter. Fold in the onion, chilli and coriander.
Cover and rest the batter for 15 minutes. Loosen with a little extra water if it's too thick to spread.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium heat and brush with some of the oil. Pour in about 1/2 cup batter and spread into a thin 18 cm round.
Cook for about 3 minutes, until set with bubbles and lifting edges. Drizzle oil around the edge, flip and cook 1–2 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Repeat with the remaining batter and oil to make 6 chillas, keeping them warm under a tea towel. Serve hot with the chutney.

batch_07.json::Filipino Chicken Inasal.title: Chicken inasal
quick_steps: Pound the garlic, lemongrass and salt to a paste. Mix with the lime juice, vinegar, soy sauce and pepper, then rub the marinade over the chicken, under the skin too.
Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour. Mix the paprika with the vegetable oil for basting.
Heat a grill plate or chargrill pan on medium. Cook the chicken skin side down for 12–15 minutes, until the skin is browned and releases easily.
Turn and cook 10–12 minutes more, brushing with the paprika oil, until the juices run clear and the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, loosely covered. Cook the rice to packet directions and serve with the chicken and pan juices.

batch_07.json::Argentinian Chimichurri S.title: Chimichurri steak
quick_steps: Mix the parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, 60 ml olive oil, oregano, chilli flakes and half the salt. Leave for 20 minutes so the flavours blend.
Pat the steak dry and rub with the remaining salt and the pepper. Rest at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Heat a heavy frying pan over high heat for 2–3 minutes until very hot, then add the remaining olive oil.
Cook the steak for 4–5 minutes without moving it, until deeply browned. Turn and cook 3–4 minutes more for medium-rare, still pink in the middle.
Rest the steak under foil for 10 minutes, then slice across the grain into 1 cm strips.
Spoon the chimichurri over the steak and serve with the resting juices.

batch_06.json::Scottish Cullen Skink.title: Cullen skink
quick_steps: Poach the haddock skin-side down in the milk, water and bay leaf over medium heat, then low, for 8–10 minutes until it flakes easily. Strain the liquid, then skin and flake the fish.
Wipe out the pan and melt the butter over medium heat. Cook the leek and onion for 6–8 minutes until soft and translucent, not browned.
Stir the potatoes through the butter for 1 minute, then add the strained liquid and simmer over medium heat.
Reduce to medium-low and simmer partly covered for 10–12 minutes until the potatoes are tender. Crush about a quarter of them to thicken the soup.
Stir in the cream and flaked haddock over low heat for 3–4 minutes until steaming hot, without boiling. Season with pepper and salt.
Stir through the parsley and serve in warm bowls.

batch_07.json::Brazilian Moqueca.title: Moqueca
quick_steps: Toss the fish with the lime juice and half the salt, then refrigerate for 15 minutes while you slice the onion, capsicum, garlic and tomatoes and chop the coriander.
Heat the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and capsicum for 6–7 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, remaining salt and pepper. Cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes start to break down.
Pour in the coconut milk and half the coriander. Simmer over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Nestle in the fish and its marinade juices. Cover and cook over low heat for 6–8 minutes until opaque and flaking easily.
Season to taste, scatter over the remaining coriander and serve from the pan.

batch_07.json::South African Bobotie.title: Bobotie
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and grease a 20 x 25 cm baking dish. Soak the torn bread in 125 ml of the milk for 10 minutes, then squeeze it, keeping the liquid.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beef mince and cook over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes, until browned and no pink remains.
Off the heat, mash in the squeezed bread, vinegar, sultanas, chutney, salt and pepper. Press the mixture firmly into the baking dish.
Whisk the eggs with the remaining milk and the reserved bread liquid. Pour over the mince and press the bay leaves onto the top.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the topping is golden and set. Rest for 5 minutes, remove the bay leaves and cut into squares.

batch_06.json::Indonesian Gado Gado.title: Gado gado
quick_steps: Boil the potatoes with the salt over high heat, then simmer on medium for 10–12 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Lift out and drain.
Cook the eggs in the same water over medium heat for 8–9 minutes until the yolks are just firm. Cool in cold water, then peel and quarter.
Boil water on high and blanch the green beans for 3 minutes, the cabbage for 1 minute, then the bean sprouts for 20 seconds. Rinse cold and drain. Slice the cucumber.
Pat the tofu dry. Fry in the vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes until golden all over. Drain.

Cook the garlic and chilli in a small saucepan over low heat for 1 minute until fragrant. Whisk in the peanut butter, kecap manis, soy sauce and 150 ml water until smooth. Off the heat, add the lime juice.
Arrange the potatoes, vegetables, tofu and eggs on a platter. Spoon the warm sauce over and serve.

batch_07.json::Turkish Lahmacun.title: Lahmacun
quick_steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, half the salt, half the olive oil and the warm water into a dough. Knead 8–10 minutes until smooth, then coat with the remaining oil, cover and prove 60 minutes until doubled.
After 45 minutes of proving, heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan) with two large oven trays inside.
Mix the lamb mince, tomatoes, capsicum, onion, garlic, tomato paste, paprika, cumin, chilli flakes, two-thirds of the parsley, remaining salt and pepper into a spreadable paste.
Divide the dough into 4 and roll each into a thin oval about 3 mm thick. Spread each with a thin layer of the lamb mixture to the edges.
Bake 2 lahmacun on the hot trays, on baking paper, for 6–8 minutes until the edges are golden and the lamb is cooked through. Repeat with the rest.
Scatter with the remaining parsley and serve hot with lemon wedges to squeeze over.

batch_07.json::Japanese Okonomiyaki.title: Okonomiyaki
quick_steps: Shred the cabbage, slice the spring onions and pat both dry. Halve the bacon, then mix the barbecue, soy and tomato sauces in a small bowl.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, then whisk in 2 eggs and the dashi until smooth and thick. Fold in the cabbage and spring onions, then stir through the remaining beaten egg.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large non-stick frypan over medium heat. Shape half the batter into a round about 2 cm thick and top with 4 bacon pieces.
Cook 5–6 minutes until the base is deep golden, then flip and cook another 5–6 minutes until the bacon and centre are cooked through and firm. Repeat with the remaining oil, batter and bacon.
Brush each pancake with the sauce mixture and drizzle with mayonnaise. Cut into 4 wedges and serve hot.

batch_07.json::Korean Gamja Jorim.title: Gamja jorim
quick_steps: Halve any larger baby potatoes, then rinse, drain and pat them dry so they brown rather than steam.
Heat the oil in a large lidded frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the potatoes cut-side down for 6–8 minutes, until golden on the edges.
Reduce to medium and add 250 ml water, the soy sauce and the mirin. Cover and simmer for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the largest potato.
Uncover, add the honey and increase to medium-high heat. Cook for 4–5 minutes, shaking the pan, until the liquid reduces to a sticky glaze.
Transfer to a serving dish and scatter with the sesame seeds. Serve warm or at room temperature.

batch_07.json::Moroccan Carrot Salad.title: Moroccan carrot salad
quick_steps: Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, paprika and most of the salt in a large bowl.
Boil a medium saucepan of water over high heat with a pinch of salt. Add the sliced carrots, reduce to medium and simmer 6–8 minutes, until just tender.
Drain the carrots well and let the steam escape for 1 minute.
Toss the warm carrots through the dressing, lightly pressing a few coins so they soak it up. Stir through the parsley.
Stand at room temperature for 30 minutes, tossing once. Add more lemon juice or salt to taste, then serve.

batch_07.json::Turkish Cilbir.title: Çılbır (Turkish eggs)
quick_steps: Let the yoghurt come to room temperature, then stir in the grated garlic and salt. Spread over four shallow bowls, leaving a slight hollow in each centre.
Bring a wide pan of water and the vinegar to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, with only small bubbles rising.
Slide in the eggs one at a time and cook 3 minutes, until the whites are set and yolks runny. Drain on paper towel.
Melt the butter in a small pan over medium-low heat. Stir in the paprika and chilli flakes for 30–60 seconds, until deep red and fragrant, then remove from the heat.
Top the yoghurt with the eggs and spoon over the warm paprika butter. Scatter with the dill and serve with the bread, toasted if you like.

batch_07.json::Spanish Gambas al Ajillo.title: Gambas al ajillo
quick_steps: Pat the prawns dry and toss with the salt. Thinly slice the garlic, chop the parsley, cut the lemon into wedges and slice the baguette.
Heat the olive oil, garlic and dried chilli in a large frying pan over low-medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until the garlic is fragrant and pale golden.
Lift the pan off the heat briefly if the garlic starts to darken, as browned garlic turns bitter.
Turn the heat to medium-high and cook the prawns in a single layer for 1–2 minutes each side, until pink, curled and opaque all the way through.
Take the pan off the heat and scatter over the parsley. Squeeze over half the lemon and serve straight away with the remaining wedges and the baguette.

batch_07.json::Italian Focaccia.title: Focaccia
quick_steps: Mix the bread flour, yeast, salt, warm water and 1 tbsp olive oil in a large bowl for 2–3 minutes, until no dry flour remains and the dough is very sticky.
Cover and rest for 30 minutes. Fold the dough over itself all the way around, rest 30 minutes, then fold again and rest 30 minutes more, until puffy and bubbly.
Spread 2 tbsp olive oil in a 20 x 30 cm tray, tip in the dough and stretch it towards the corners. Cover and rest 40 minutes, until doubled and airy.
About 15 minutes before the rise ends, heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Drizzle with the remaining olive oil, press deep dimples all over with oiled fingertips, then scatter over the rosemary and flaky sea salt.
Bake for 22–25 minutes, until deep golden and the base is crisp. Rest in the tray 5 minutes, then cool on a wire rack 5 minutes and cut.

batch_07.json::Turkish Simit.title: Simit (sesame bread rings)
quick_steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the warm water and olive oil. Knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and leave in a warm spot for about 60 minutes, until doubled in size.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line two trays. Whisk the honey with 100 ml water, spread the sesame seeds in a dish, and divide the dough into 8.
Roll each piece into a 60 cm rope, fold in half, twist and pinch into a ring. Dip in the honey mixture, then coat both sides in sesame seeds.
Bake for 18–20 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until deep golden and the base sounds hollow. Cool on a rack for 10 minutes.

batch_07.json::Italian Caprese Panini.title: Caprese panini
quick_steps: Slice the mozzarella and tomatoes into 5 mm pieces, and pick the basil leaves.
Lay the mozzarella and tomato on paper towel, sprinkle the tomato with the salt and leave for 10 minutes. Pat dry.
Halve the ciabatta rolls and spread the pesto over the cut sides, 1 tbsp per roll.
Layer the mozzarella, tomato and basil on the bottom halves, add black pepper, close the rolls and brush the outsides with the olive oil.
Toast 2 paninis at a time in a press on medium-high for 4–5 minutes, until golden and the mozzarella has started to melt.
Toast the remaining 2, then rest all four for 1 minute before cutting in half.

batch_07.json::Middle Eastern Mujadara.title: Mujadara
quick_steps: Simmer the rinsed lentils in 750 ml water over medium-low heat for 18–20 minutes until almost tender, then drain, reserving 400 ml of the cooking water.
Cook the onions in 2 tbsp of the olive oil and half the salt in a large pan over medium heat for 25 minutes until deep golden. Set half aside for topping.
Stir the remaining oil and the cumin through the pan onions over medium heat for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lentils, rinsed rice, remaining salt and reserved water. Boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes until the rice is tender. Rest 5 minutes.
Mix the Greek yoghurt with the lemon zest, 1 tbsp of the juice and a pinch of black pepper.
Fluff the rice, season with pepper and extra lemon juice, then top with the reserved onions and serve with the lemon yoghurt.

batch_07.json::British Ploughman's Lunch.title: Ploughman's lunch
quick_steps: Leave the cheddar on the bench, still wrapped, for 10 minutes. Spoon the chutney into a small bowl and set the butter out to soften.
Wash the cucumber and radishes. Trim the radishes and halve them lengthways, cut the cucumber into 7 cm batons, and drain the pickled onions.
Cut the cheddar into 4 thick wedges. Core the apples and cut into 8 wedges each, toss in the lemon juice and 250 ml water for 30 seconds, then drain.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Warm the bread slices on the rack for 5 minutes, until the crust is crisp, then spread with the butter.
Divide the cheese, apple, cucumber, radishes and pickled onions among 4 plates or a board. Add a spoonful of chutney and serve with the warm bread.

batch_07.json::Turkish Sutlac.title: Sütlaç (rice pudding)
quick_steps: Rinse the arborio rice until the water runs mostly clear. Whisk the cornflour with 100 ml of the milk until smooth, and set out four 250 ml ramekins on a tray.
Boil the rice with 250 ml water over medium-high heat, then cover and simmer on medium-low for 10–12 minutes, until tender and the water is absorbed.
Add the remaining 800 ml milk and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Stir in the caster sugar, then cook on medium-low for 20–25 minutes, until the rice is very soft and slightly thickened.
Stir in the cornflour mixture and cook over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Off the heat, stir in the vanilla extract and divide among the ramekins.
Grill on high, 10 cm from the element, for 3–5 minutes, until the tops are speckled golden brown.
Cool on the bench for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for at least 2½ hours, until completely cold and set.

batch_07.json::Vietnamese Bun Cha.title: Bún chả
quick_steps: Mix the pork mince with half the garlic, the spring onions, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and the black pepper until sticky. Shape into 16 small patties and chill for 30 minutes.
Cut one carrot into matchsticks and slice the other into rounds. Dissolve the remaining sugar in 250 ml warm water, then add the remaining fish sauce, lime juice, rice vinegar and remaining garlic.
Add the chilli and carrot rounds to the broth and leave to pickle while you cook.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the patties in two batches, 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply browned and no longer pink in the centre, then add them to the broth.
Cook the rice vermicelli to the packet directions, then drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Serve the noodles with torn lettuce, mint leaves and carrot matchsticks on a platter, with the patties in broth alongside.

batch_07.json::Mexican Arroz con Leche.title: Arroz con leche
quick_steps: Rinse the rice and drain. Peel 2 wide strips of zest from the orange, avoiding the white pith.
Bring the water, cinnamon stick and salt to the boil in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the rice, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until the water is almost absorbed.
Add the milk and orange zest. Simmer over medium-low heat, stirring often, for about 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the mixture coats a spoon.
Stir in the condensed milk and vanilla. Simmer on low for 5 minutes, until glossy.
Remove the cinnamon stick and zest, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes to thicken.
Spoon into bowls and dust with the ground cinnamon. Serve warm or chilled.

batch_07.json::Italian Zabaglione.title: Zabaglione
quick_steps: Divide the strawberries among 4 serving glasses. Bring the water to a gentle simmer in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat.
Whisk the egg yolks and caster sugar in a large heatproof bowl for 2–3 minutes, until pale and slightly thickened. Whisk in the marsala.
Set the bowl over the barely simmering water, base clear of the water. Whisk constantly for 8–10 minutes, until tripled in volume, thick, foamy and warm.
If the edges look scrambled, lift the bowl off the heat and whisk hard for 10 seconds before returning it.
Spoon the warm zabaglione over the strawberries and serve straight away.

batch_07.json::Indian Gulab Jamun.title: Gulab jamun
quick_steps: Lightly crush the cardamom. Simmer the sugar, 300 ml water and cardamom in a saucepan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, until slightly sticky but still runny. Stir in the rosewater and keep warm on low.
Whisk the milk powder, flour and baking powder, then rub in the butter until it looks like fine crumbs. Add the milk gradually to form a soft, slightly tacky dough and rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Lightly oil your palms with a little of the vegetable oil. Divide the dough into 16 pieces and roll each into a smooth ball with no cracks.

Heat the rest of the oil in a deep saucepan over low-medium heat to about 140°C. Fry the balls in batches for 8–10 minutes, until deep golden and puffed, with a skewer coming out clean from the centre.
Drain the balls briefly on paper towel, then add them to the warm syrup. Soak off the heat for at least 30 minutes, until swollen and soft through, then serve 4 per person.

batch_07.json::Japanese Dorayaki.title: Dorayaki
quick_steps: Whisk the eggs, caster sugar and honey for 2–3 minutes until pale, thick and foamy. Whisk in the water, then sift in the flour and baking powder and fold until just smooth.
Cover and rest the batter for 20 minutes. Meanwhile, divide the red bean paste into 4 portions and shape each into a flat disc about 6 cm wide.
Heat a large non-stick pan over low–medium heat and wipe with a little vegetable oil. Cook 3 tbsp batter rounds for 2–3 minutes until bubbles form and edges look set.
Flip and cook 1 minute until golden and springy. Cool on a wire rack, repeating to make 8 pancakes, re-oiling the pan lightly between batches.
Cool the pancakes for 3–4 minutes. Spread a bean paste disc on the paler side of one pancake, leaving a 1 cm border, then top with another pancake, golden side up, pressing the edges together.

batch_07.json::Georgian Lobio.title: Lobio
quick_steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until fragrant and lightly browned. Cool, then chop very finely or pound to a coarse paste.
Heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Cook the onion with 1/4 tsp of the salt for 12–15 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in half the garlic and the coriander and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the kidney beans and 250 ml water, bring to the boil, then simmer on low, partly covered, for 30 minutes until very tender and thickened.
About 20 minutes in, mash a third of the beans to make it creamy. Add 60 ml water if it looks dry.
Stir in the walnuts, remaining garlic and 1/2 tsp salt and simmer on low for 5 minutes until thick. Season with pepper and rest for 5 minutes.

batch_07.json::American Key Lime Pie.title: Key lime pie
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan). Blitz the digestive biscuits to fine crumbs, mix with the melted butter and press into a 20 cm pie dish.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes, until lightly golden at the edges and firm to touch. Keep the oven on.
Whisk the egg yolks for 1–2 minutes until pale and slightly thick. Whisk in the condensed milk, lime juice and lime zest, then pour into the warm crust.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre still wobbles slightly. Cool in the dish for 30 minutes.
Cover and chill for 3 hours or overnight, until firm in the centre. Chill the cream bowl for the last 15 minutes.
Whisk the thickened cream and icing sugar in the chilled bowl until soft peaks form, about 2–3 minutes. Spread over the pie and serve cold.

batch_07.json::Sri Lankan Dhal Curry.title: Sri Lankan dhal curry
quick_steps: Rinse the red lentils until the water runs almost clear. Put them in a medium saucepan with one chopped onion, the slit chilli, garlic, turmeric, 6 curry leaves and 750 ml water.
Bring to the boil over high heat, skimming off any foam. Reduce to medium-low and simmer for 15–18 minutes until the lentils are soft and falling apart, then stir in the salt.
Pour in the coconut milk and warm over low heat for 4–5 minutes until hot and creamy, without boiling hard. Loosen with a splash of water if thicker than a loose porridge.
Heat the oil in a small frying pan over medium heat. Cook the mustard seeds for 30–60 seconds until they pop.
Add the sliced onion and chopped chilli and cook for 4–5 minutes until golden. Add the remaining 6 curry leaves and cook 30 seconds until crisp.
Stir the tempering through the dhal and serve with lime wedges.

batch_07.json::Cuban Ropa Vieja.title: Ropa vieja
quick_steps: Pat the beef dry and season with the salt and pepper. Slice the onion and capsicums and chop the garlic.
Brown the beef in the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat, 3–4 minutes per side until deeply golden. Set aside.
Reduce to medium and cook the onion and capsicums for 6–7 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, cumin, oregano and tomato paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, stock and bay leaves, scraping up the browned bits. Return the beef, cover and cook on low for 2 hours until it shreds easily.
Discard the bay leaves and shred the beef. Return it to the pot with the olives and vinegar and simmer uncovered on medium for 10–15 minutes until the sauce is thick.
Season to taste with extra salt, stir through half the coriander and scatter the rest on top.

batch_07.json::Persian Fesenjan.title: Fesenjan
quick_steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until fragrant. Cool, then pulse in a food processor until finely ground and sandy.
Season the chicken with the salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken in two batches, 3–4 minutes each, until golden. Set aside.
Reduce to medium and cook the onion in the same pot for 6–7 minutes until soft and lightly golden.

Stir in the walnuts and cinnamon for 1 minute, then add the stock, scraping up the browned bits. Return the chicken and juices, cover with the lid slightly ajar, and simmer on low for 30 minutes until cooked through.
Stir in the pomegranate molasses and the sugar, if using. Simmer uncovered on low for 15 minutes until thick, glossy and dark, cooking the rice meanwhile.
Adjust with extra sugar if too sour or a pinch of salt if flat, then serve over the rice.

batch_07.json::Swedish Cinnamon Buns.title: Swedish cinnamon buns
quick_steps: Warm the milk and 50 g of the butter in a saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes, until the butter melts and the milk is lukewarm.
Mix the flour, 50 g of the caster sugar, yeast, cardamom and salt, add the milk mixture and knead 8–10 minutes until smooth. Rise covered in a warm spot for 1 hour, until doubled.
Mix 50 g soft butter, the remaining 40 g caster sugar and the cinnamon into a paste. Roll the dough into a 30 x 40 cm rectangle, spread with the paste, roll up and slice into 12 rounds.
Place the buns cut side up on two lined trays, cover and rest in a warm spot for 30 minutes, until puffy. Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) for the last 15 minutes.
Brush with the beaten egg and bake for 10–12 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until deep golden and hollow-sounding underneath.
Brush with the remaining 30 g melted butter, sprinkle with the white sugar and cool on the trays for 10 minutes.

batch_07.json::Greek Galaktoboureko.title: Galaktoboureko
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease a 20 x 25 cm dish with a little of the melted butter, strip the zest from the lemon and juice it, and keep the filo under a damp tea towel.
Whisk the milk, semolina and half the sugar in a saucepan over medium heat for 8–10 minutes until thick. Off the heat, stir in the vanilla, cool 5 minutes, then whisk in the eggs.
Layer 5 buttered filo sheets in the dish, letting the edges overhang. Pour in the custard, fold the edges over, then top with 5 more buttered sheets.
Tuck in the edges, brush with the remaining butter and score into squares. Bake 35–40 minutes until deep golden and just set with a slight wobble.
Meanwhile, simmer the water, remaining sugar, zest strips and 1 tbsp lemon juice over medium heat for 8 minutes until slightly syrupy. Remove the zest and cool.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot pastry and rest at least 30 minutes. Cut along the scored lines and serve warm or at room temperature.

batch_07.json::Nepalese Chicken Momo.title: Chicken momo
quick_steps: Mix the flour and half the salt with the water, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth and firm. Cover with a damp tea towel and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the chicken mince, spring onions, ginger, garlic, onion, coriander, soy sauce, cumin, pepper, remaining salt and oil by hand until sticky and well combined.
Divide the dough into 24 pieces and roll each into a thin 9 cm circle, with the edges thinner than the centre.
Put 1 tablespoon of filling in each circle, then pleat and pinch the edge to seal fully, twisting the top closed.
Bring water to the boil in a wok or pot over high heat. Arrange the momo in a lined or oiled steamer, 2 cm apart, and set it over the water on medium-high.
Steam in batches for 12–15 minutes, until the dough is translucent and the chicken is cooked through with no pink remaining. Serve hot.

batch_07.json::Indonesian Soto Ayam.title: Soto ayam
quick_steps: Crush the garlic, grate the ginger, bruise the lemongrass, shred the cabbage, slice the spring onions and cut the limes into wedges.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the garlic, ginger and lemongrass for 1–2 minutes until fragrant, then the turmeric for 30 seconds until the oil turns golden.
Add the stock, 750 ml water and salt, and bring to the boil over high heat. Add the chicken thigh, reduce to low and simmer, partly covered, for 25–30 minutes until cooked through and no longer pink.
Lift out the chicken, discard the lemongrass and keep the broth hot over low heat. Shred the chicken with two forks.
Cook the rice vermicelli in a separate pot of boiling water to the packet directions, then drain and rinse. Simmer the cabbage in the broth over medium heat for 1 minute until just wilted.
Divide the vermicelli among four bowls, top with the chicken, and ladle over the broth and cabbage. Scatter with the spring onions and serve with the lime wedges.

batch_07.json::Greek Lemon Chicken Orzo.title: Lemon chicken orzo
quick_steps: Zest and juice the lemon separately, dice the onion and crush the garlic. Toss the chicken thighs with the oregano, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large deep lidded frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken 4–5 minutes per side until deeply golden, then set aside.
Reduce to medium, add the remaining oil and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic and zest for 30 seconds, then the orzo for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and remaining salt, scraping up the browned bits, and bring to a simmer. Nestle the chicken back in with its juices.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12–14 minutes, until the orzo is tender and the chicken has no pink in the centre. Rest the chicken for 5 minutes.
Stir the spinach and lemon juice through the orzo over low heat for 1–2 minutes until wilted and saucy. Slice the chicken, serve on top and season to taste.

batch_07.json::Malaysian Char Kway Teow.title: Char kway teow
quick_steps: Separate the noodles, warming them briefly in the microwave if stiff. Whisk both soy sauces, sugar and pepper in a bowl, and beat the eggs separately.
Heat a wok on high until just smoking. Stir-fry the prawns in 1 tbsp oil for 1–2 minutes until pink and curled, then set aside.
Scramble the eggs in 1 tbsp oil for about 30 seconds until just set, then move them to the prawns.
Stir-fry the garlic and chilli flakes in the remaining oil for 15 seconds until fragrant. Toss in the noodles and sauce for 2–3 minutes until dark, hot and slightly charred.
Return the prawns and eggs, add the bean sprouts, spring onions and chives, and toss for 1 minute until the sprouts just wilt and the prawns are cooked through. Serve immediately.
batch_07.json::Malaysian Char Kway Teow.hand_fixed: drift judge flag, fixed by hand (approved 2026-11-20)

batch_07.json::Japanese Kinpira Gobo.title: Kinpira gobo
quick_steps: Scrub the burdock and cut it and the carrots into 5 cm matchsticks. Soak the burdock in 1 litre water with the white vinegar for 10 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, white sugar and 1 tbsp water in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the vegetable oil and sesame oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Stir-fry the burdock for 3–4 minutes, until nutty and softening at the edges.
Add the carrots and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until bright and just tender.
Pour in the sauce, reduce to medium and cook for 3–4 minutes, until almost evaporated and glossy. Off the heat, stir through the sesame seeds and serve.

batch_07.json::German Rotkohl.title: Rotkohl
quick_steps: Shred the red cabbage finely. Peel, core and coarsely grate the apples and toss through the cabbage. Slice the onion thinly.
Melt the butter in a large heavy-based saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion with the salt for 5–6 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the cabbage and apple and stir for 2 minutes until the cabbage starts to wilt.
Add the vinegar, sugar, cloves and water. Bring to a simmer, then reduce to low, cover and cook 35–40 minutes until the cabbage is very tender.
Uncover, increase to medium and cook 3–5 minutes until the liquid has mostly evaporated and the cabbage looks glossy.
Remove the cloves, season with the pepper, adjust the sugar or vinegar to taste, and serve hot.

batch_07.json::Korean Gyeran Bap.title: Gyeran bap
quick_steps: Cut the nori into thin strips, slice the spring onions, and mix the soy sauce and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Microwave the rice on high for 2–3 minutes until steaming hot. Divide among 4 bowls and dot each with butter to melt in.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Fry the eggs for 2–3 minutes until the edges are crisp and golden and the whites are set.
Flip for 30 seconds if you like firmer yolks. Slide one egg onto each bowl of rice.
Spoon the soy and sesame mixture over, then scatter with nori and spring onions. Break the yolk and stir through the hot rice.

batch_07.json::Tunisian Brik.title: Brik
quick_steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water over high heat, then simmer on medium for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain and steam dry for 5 minutes.
Coarsely mash the potatoes, leaving small lumps, then mix in the tuna, parsley, capers, lemon zest and pepper. Divide into 4 portions.
Fold a filo sheet in half (or stack 2 if thin). Shape a portion of filling into a ring with a well, then crack an egg into the well.
Fold the pastry into a half-moon and press the edges to seal. Repeat with the remaining filo, filling and eggs.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until a pinch of pastry sizzles. Fry the briks one at a time, 1–2 minutes a side, until golden and the egg white is set.
Drain on paper towel and serve straight away with the lemon wedges.

batch_07.json::Syrian Muhammara.title: Muhammara
quick_steps: Roast the whole capsicums at 220°C (200°C fan) for 30–35 minutes, turning once, until blistered, blackened in patches and soft. Cover them in a bowl to steam.
Lower the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and toast the walnuts for 6–8 minutes until fragrant and a shade darker, then cool for 10 minutes.
Once the capsicums have steamed for at least 15 minutes, peel them and discard the stems and seeds. Drain the flesh in a sieve for 5 minutes.
Pulse the walnuts and breadcrumbs until coarsely ground. Add the capsicum, pomegranate molasses, garlic, salt, chilli flakes, cumin and lemon juice, then blend until thick but slightly textured.
With the motor running, drizzle in 1 tbsp olive oil, then taste and adjust the salt and lemon juice.
Spoon into a shallow bowl, swirl the top, drizzle with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and serve at room temperature.

batch_07.json::French Lentil Salad with.title: French lentil salad with goat cheese
quick_steps: Rinse the lentils and simmer with the bay leaf in 750 ml water over medium-low heat for 20–25 minutes, until tender but still holding their shape.
Drain the lentils, discard the bay leaf and let them steam dry for 2 minutes.
Soak the diced shallots in the red wine vinegar for 5 minutes, then whisk in the mustard, olive oil, salt and pepper until thick.
Toss the warm lentils through the dressing and leave for 5 minutes.
Fold through the chopped parsley and adjust the salt or vinegar to taste.
Divide among 4 bowls and top with the crumbled goat cheese.

batch_07.json::Turkish Mercimek Corbasi.title: Mercimek çorbası (red lentil soup)
quick_steps: Rinse the red lentils until the water runs mostly clear. Finely chop the onion and garlic, dice the carrot small, and cut the lemon into wedges.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and salt for 6–7 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, cumin and paprika for 1 minute, until fragrant and the paste darkens slightly.
Add the lentils, vegetable stock and 750 ml water. Bring to the boil over high heat and skim off any foam.
Reduce to medium-low and simmer, partly covered, for 18–20 minutes until the lentils have collapsed and the carrot is very tender.
Blend the soup until completely smooth, then warm it over low heat for 2–3 minutes. Season with black pepper and extra salt, and serve with the lemon wedges.

batch_07.json::Israeli Sabich Pita.title: Sabich pita
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss 1 cm eggplant rounds with the olive oil and half the salt, then roast on a lined tray for 30–35 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and very soft.
Boil the eggs in a saucepan over medium heat for 10 minutes, until the yolks are firm. Cool in cold water for 5 minutes, then peel and slice.
Combine the tomatoes, cucumber and parsley with a quarter teaspoon of salt and a pinch of black pepper.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and remaining salt, then whisk in 80 ml water until smooth and pourable like thick cream.
Warm the pita in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 30 seconds each side, until soft. Cut open a pocket in each.
Fill the pita with eggplant, egg and salad, drizzle generously with the tahini sauce and serve straight away.

batch_07.json::Colombian Arepas con Ques.title: Arepas con queso
quick_steps: Whisk the cornmeal and salt in a large bowl. Mix in the warm water and 15 g of the butter by hand, then knead 2 minutes until soft and smooth.
Cover and rest the dough for 5 minutes. Knead in the grated mozzarella for 2 minutes until evenly distributed.
Divide into 8 balls and flatten each into a disc about 1.5 cm thick and 8 cm wide, pinching any cracks smooth.
Melt half the remaining butter in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook 4 arepas for 7 minutes until golden, then flip and cook 6 minutes more until golden and hollow-sounding.
Wipe the pan, melt the last of the butter over medium heat and cook the other 4 arepas the same way, 7 minutes then 6 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding. Serve hot.

batch_07.json::Brazilian Brigadeiros.title: Brigadeiros
quick_steps: Grease a large plate with some of the extra butter. Tip the sprinkles into a shallow bowl.
Combine the condensed milk, cocoa and 25 g butter in a small heavy-based saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir until the butter melts and the cocoa dissolves, about 2 minutes.
Keep stirring and scraping the base for 10–12 minutes, until thick and glossy and a spoon leaves a trail that takes 2–3 seconds to close.
Pour onto the greased plate and spread evenly. Cool at room temperature for about 40 minutes, until firm enough to roll.
Rub your hands with the remaining butter, then roll tablespoons of mixture into balls. Coat each in sprinkles until evenly covered and serve.

batch_07.json::Thai Khanom Krok.title: Khanom krok
quick_steps: Whisk the rice flour, half the coconut milk, the water, 2 tbsp of the sugar and a pinch of the salt until smooth and pourable. Rest for 10 minutes.
Warm the remaining coconut milk, sugar and salt in a small saucepan over low heat for 3–4 minutes, until the sugar dissolves and it's just steaming. Keep warm and slice the spring onions.
Heat a mini round-welled pancake pan over medium-low heat for 3 minutes and brush the wells with oil. Fill each well two-thirds full with batter.
Cook uncovered for 3–4 minutes, until the edges are set and lift away from the pan.
Spoon the warm coconut topping into each pancake and scatter over the spring onions. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes, until the topping is set and the bases are golden and crisp.
Loosen, lift out and serve warm. Re-oil the wells and repeat with the remaining batter.

batch_07.json::Mexican Tostadas de Tinga.title: Tostadas de tinga
quick_steps: Thinly slice the onion. Chop the garlic, tomatoes and chipotle chillies. Shred the chicken and lettuce, crumble the feta and cut the lime into wedges.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Cook the garlic, oregano and cumin for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the tomatoes and chipotle and simmer for 10 minutes until broken down and soft.
Blend the mixture until smooth, then return it to the pan. Stir in the chicken and salt and simmer on medium-low for 10–12 minutes until thick and hot through.
Pile the chicken onto the tostadas, two per plate. Top with the lettuce and feta and serve straight away with the lime wedges.

batch_07.json::Portuguese Açorda Alentej.title: Açorda alentejana
quick_steps: Divide the torn bread among 4 wide bowls. Pound the garlic with the salt into a paste, then pound in the coriander, olive oil and a good grind of pepper.
Bring the stock to a simmer in a large wide saucepan over medium heat, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic and coriander paste and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the vinegar and drop the heat to medium-low so the broth barely bubbles. Crack in the eggs and poach 3–4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks runny.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon and keep the broth hot.
Ladle the hot broth over the bread and leave 1–2 minutes until softened. Top each bowl with an egg and serve.

batch_07.json::Hungarian Chicken Paprika.title: Chicken paprikash
quick_steps: Cut each chicken thigh into 2–3 large pieces and season with the salt and pepper. Chop the onions, garlic, tomatoes and parsley.
Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken in batches for 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden, then set aside.
Reduce to medium and cook the onions for 8–10 minutes until very soft and golden, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Take the pot off the heat for 30 seconds, then stir in the paprika and flour. Return to medium heat for 1 minute.
Stir in the stock and tomatoes, return the chicken and juices, then simmer covered with the lid slightly ajar over medium-low heat for 20–25 minutes, until cooked through with no pink near the bone.
Off the heat, temper the sour cream with 3 tbsp of the hot sauce and stir it in. Warm over low heat for 2–3 minutes without boiling, season to taste and scatter with parsley.

batch_07.json::Danish Smorrebrod with Sm.title: Smørrebrød with smoked salmon
quick_steps: Slice the cucumber into thin ribbons, toss with the salt and leave for 10 minutes.
Zest the lemon, juice half and cut the other half into 4 wedges. Chop the dill, keeping 4 sprigs for garnish.
Beat the cream cheese until smooth, then mix in the lemon zest, 2 tsp lemon juice, chopped dill and black pepper. Add more juice if you want it sharper.
Pat the cucumber dry. Spread the rye bread thinly with butter right to the edges, then cover with the lemon dill cream cheese.
Drape the smoked salmon over in loose waves and top with the cucumber.
Garnish with a dill sprig and a grind of black pepper, and serve with a lemon wedge.

batch_07.json::German Kaiserschmarrn.title: Kaiserschmarrn
quick_steps: Whisk the egg yolks, milk and vanilla, then whisk in the flour and salt until smooth. Beat the egg whites with 40 g of the caster sugar to soft peaks and fold them in.
Rest the batter for 10 minutes. Meanwhile, simmer the berries with 1 tbsp caster sugar in a small saucepan over medium-low heat for 4–5 minutes, until soft and juicy.
Melt half the butter in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour in the batter and cook for 5–6 minutes, until golden underneath and mostly set.
Cut into quarters, flip and cook for 3–4 minutes more, until golden and cooked through with no raw batter in the centre.
Add the remaining butter, tear the pancake into chunks and sprinkle over the remaining caster sugar. Cook over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes, until golden and caramelised.
Divide among four plates, dust with icing sugar and serve straight away with the warm berries.

batch_08.json::Moroccan Chicken Tagine w.title: Moroccan chicken tagine with preserved lemon
quick_steps: Rub the chicken with the salt, ginger and turmeric. Slice the onions, chop the garlic, strip the rinsed preserved lemon rind, and soak the saffron in the stock.
Brown the chicken in the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat, 6–7 minutes skin-side down until deep golden, then 2 minutes more. Set aside.
Cook the onions in the same pot over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the saffron stock, scraping up the browned bits. Return the chicken skin-side up and simmer gently, covered, on low for 20 minutes.
Add the preserved lemon and olives and cook covered for 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink near the bone.
Uncover and simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes until glossy and thickened. Cook the couscous to packet directions, then serve the tagine over it with the coriander.

batch_07.json::Turkish Revani.title: Revani
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease and line a 20 cm square tin with butter and baking paper, and zest 1 lemon.
Whisk the eggs and 120 g of the sugar for 4–5 minutes, until pale, thick and doubled. Whisk in the melted butter, yoghurt, milk and lemon zest.
Fold in the semolina, flour and baking powder until just combined. Pour into the tin, rest 10 minutes, then bake 30–35 minutes, until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Meanwhile, juice both lemons and simmer the juice with the remaining 180 g sugar and 300 ml water over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, until slightly syrupy. Cool completely.
Cut the hot cake into 16 pieces right through to the base. Slowly ladle the cooled syrup over it.
Sprinkle with the coconut and rest for at least 30 minutes, until the syrup is absorbed and the cake has cooled.

batch_08.json::Jamaican Jerk Chicken.title: Jerk chicken
quick_steps: Blend the spring onions, garlic, deseeded Scotch bonnet (wear gloves), allspice, thyme, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar and oil into a rough paste, about 30–45 seconds.
Slash the dried drumsticks 2–3 times, then rub the paste into the slashes and under the skin. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Bring the chicken out 20 minutes before cooking. Heat a lidded barbecue to medium (180°C) for indirect cooking, or the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Cook the drumsticks skin side up on the indirect side or an oven rack, lid closed, turning every 10 minutes for 35 minutes, until deeply browned and cooked through with clear juices (75°C).
Char over direct medium-high heat or under a hot grill for 3–5 minutes, turning often, until spotted with char.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with the lime wedges.

batch_08.json::Turkish İmam Bayıldı.title: İmam bayıldı
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Halve the eggplants, slit the cut faces, brush with 2 tbsp olive oil and half the salt, then roast cut-side up for 25 minutes, until golden and soft.
Meanwhile, cook the onions in 2 tbsp olive oil in a large pan over medium heat for 10 minutes, until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, sugar, remaining salt and pepper. Cook 8–10 minutes until thick and jammy, then stir in half the parsley.
Hollow out the eggplants, spoon in the filling and pack into a baking dish. Pour in the water and drizzle with the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil.
Cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes, until very tender and collapsing when pressed.
Rest covered for 5 minutes. Spoon the juices over, drizzle with the lemon juice and scatter with the remaining parsley.

batch_08.json::Sichuan Mapo Tofu.title: Sichuan mapo tofu
quick_steps: Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry wok over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, until fragrant, then crush coarsely. Mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp cold water until smooth.
