Simmer the tofu in 1 litre of salted water in a saucepan over medium heat for 2 minutes, then drain gently.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork mince for 4–5 minutes, until browned and no longer pink.
Reduce to medium and fry the doubanjiang and black beans for 1 minute, until the oil turns red. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the stock and tofu and simmer for 5 minutes. Pour in about half the cornflour mixture and simmer for 1 minute, until the sauce lightly coats the tofu.
Scatter over the crushed peppercorns and spring onions, and serve straight away with cooked rice.

batch_08.json::Japanese Miso-Glazed Aube.title: Miso-glazed eggplant
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan). Halve the eggplants, score the flesh in a diamond pattern, then brush with the oil and sprinkle with the salt.
Roast cut-side up for 25 minutes, until very soft and lightly browned.
Meanwhile, whisk the miso, mirin, sugar and soy sauce until smooth, and cook the rice according to the packet.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until golden.
Spread the miso mixture over the eggplants and grill on high for 3–4 minutes, until bubbling and spotted dark brown. Rest for 2 minutes.
Serve the eggplants over the rice, scattered with the spring onions and sesame seeds.

batch_08.json::Greek Lemon Chicken and P.title: Greek lemon chicken and potatoes
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the potato wedges in a large roasting dish, nestle the chicken thighs among them skin side up, and season with the salt and pepper.
Juice the lemons into a jug and whisk in the olive oil, garlic, oregano, paprika and chicken stock. Pour over the chicken and potatoes, turning the potatoes to coat.
Roast for 25 minutes, then turn the potatoes and spoon the pan juices over the chicken.
Roast for another 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when pierced and the chicken skin is golden.
Increase the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and roast for 10 minutes, until the potato edges are golden. Check the thickest thigh is cooked through, with no pink meat and clear juices.
Rest for 5 minutes, then spoon the pan juices over to serve.

batch_08.json::Mexican Pozole Rojo.title: Pozole rojo
quick_steps: Toast the chillies in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 20–30 seconds per side, until fragrant. Soak in 500 ml boiling water for 20 minutes, until soft.
Shred the cabbage, slice the radishes and cut the lime into wedges for serving.

Bring the pork, half the onion, stock, salt and 500 ml water to the boil in a large pot over high heat. Reduce to medium-low, skim off the foam and simmer partly covered for 1 hour, until almost tender.
Blend the drained chillies with the garlic, remaining onion, oregano and 250 ml hot broth until completely smooth. Sieve into the pot.
Add the hominy and simmer partly covered over medium-low heat for 30 minutes, until the pork is very tender. Shred the pork, return it to the pot and simmer 5 minutes more, then season.
Ladle into bowls and top with the cabbage, radishes and a pinch of extra oregano. Serve with the lime wedges.

batch_08.json::French Chicken Chasseur.title: Chicken chasseur
quick_steps: Pat the chicken dry and season with the salt and pepper. Slice the mushrooms, chop the shallots, garlic and tarragon, and lightly drain the canned tomatoes.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a large deep pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken skin-side down until deep golden, then turn and brown the other side. Set aside.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp fat. Over medium heat, cook the mushrooms in the remaining butter until browned, then add the shallots and garlic until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour for 1 minute. Add the wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Add the stock and tomatoes and bring to a simmer. Return the chicken skin-side up with its juices, cover and cook on medium-low for 20 minutes.
Uncover and simmer 5 minutes more, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is cooked through with clear juices. Stir through half the tarragon and scatter the rest over.

batch_08.json::Spanish Albóndigas in Tom.title: Albóndigas in tomato sauce
quick_steps: Combine the beef and pork mince, egg, breadcrumbs, half the garlic, half the parsley, 3/4 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Roll into about 24 walnut-sized balls.
Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs in two batches, 5–6 minutes each, until browned all over, then set aside.
Reduce to medium and add the remaining oil. Cook the onion with the remaining salt for 5–6 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in the remaining garlic and the smoked paprika for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the passata and 125 ml water, scraping up the browned bits.
Simmer for 8 minutes until slightly thickened. Return the meatballs and their juices, partly cover and simmer on low for 20–25 minutes, until cooked through with no pink inside.
Sprinkle with the remaining parsley and serve with the sliced baguette.

batch_08.json::Polish Bigos Hunter's Ste.title: Bigos (hunter's stew)
quick_steps: Toss the pork with the salt and pepper. Brown in half the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat, in two batches, until deeply golden. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil and reduce to medium. Cook the onion until soft, then the mushrooms until their liquid mostly evaporates, about 8 minutes.
Add the sausage and cook 2 minutes until lightly browned. Stir in the cabbage, sauerkraut, caraway and bay leaves until the cabbage starts to wilt.
Return the pork and juices to the pot with the stock, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a gentle boil, then cover and simmer on low for 90 minutes, until the pork is very tender.
Uncover and simmer on medium for 20 minutes until thick and moist, not soupy. Remove the bay leaves, season to taste and rest 5 minutes.

batch_08.json::Tunisian Harissa Baked Fi.title: Harissa baked fish
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the capsicums and red onion with 2 tbsp olive oil, the cumin and half the salt on a large tray.
Roast the vegetables for 20 minutes, stirring halfway, until softened and starting to colour at the edges.
Meanwhile, pat the fish dry and season with the remaining salt. Mix the harissa with the juice of half the lemon and 1 tbsp olive oil, then brush it over the fish.
Nestle the fish among the vegetables and scatter on the cherry tomatoes. Bake for 12–15 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily and the tomatoes have split.
Meanwhile, cover the couscous with 250 ml boiling water for 5 minutes, then fluff. Serve with the fish and vegetables, scattered with parsley and with the lemon wedges.

batch_08.json::Japanese Onigiri with Tun.title: Onigiri with tuna mayo
quick_steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs almost clear, then drain for 5 minutes. Bring it to the boil with the water over high heat in a lidded saucepan.
Reduce to low, cover and cook for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed. Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff.
Flake the drained tuna into a bowl and stir through the mayonnaise and soy sauce until creamy. Cut the nori sheets into 12 strips.
Spread the rice on a tray for about 5 minutes until warm but no longer steaming. Dissolve the salt in a small bowl of water for wetting your hands.
Press a hollow into a quarter cup of rice, add a heaped teaspoon of filling, then enclose and press into a triangle. Make 12.
Wrap a nori strip around the base of each onigiri just before serving at room temperature.

batch_08.json::Chinese Steamed Ginger Fi.title: Steamed ginger fish
quick_steps: Cut the ginger, spring onions and coriander as directed. Pat the fish dry, rub with the salt, and lay on a heatproof rimmed plate with half the ginger and spring onion.
Mix the soy sauce and Shaoxing wine in a jug and set aside until the fish has steamed. Cook the rice according to the packet.
Boil 3 cm of water in a wok or pot over high heat. Set the plate on the rack, cover, and steam over medium heat 8–10 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Pour away the milky liquid. Top the fish with the remaining ginger and spring onion, then pour the soy mixture around it.
Heat the vegetable oil in a small saucepan over high heat 1–2 minutes until it just begins to smoke, then pour it over the fish so it sizzles.
Drizzle with the sesame oil, top with the coriander and serve at once with the rice.

batch_08.json::Swedish Overnight Oats wi.title: Swedish overnight oats with berries
quick_steps: Toast the almonds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until golden and fragrant. Cool, then roughly chop.
Combine the oats and cardamom in a large bowl. Stir in the milk, greek yoghurt and honey until no dry oats remain.
Divide between four jars, cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight, until soft and creamy.
Keep the chopped almonds covered at room temperature so they stay crisp.
Stir each jar and loosen with the extra milk, 1 tbsp at a time, until spoonable. Top with the blueberries and almonds and serve cold.

batch_08.json::Vietnamese Rice Paper Rol.title: Rice paper rolls
quick_steps: Soak the vermicelli in just-boiled water for 5–6 minutes, until soft and no longer opaque. Drain, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into fine matchsticks, tear the lettuce, pick the mint and coriander, and halve the prawns lengthways.
Warm the hoisin and peanut butter in a small saucepan over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until smooth. Off the heat, whisk in 80 ml warm water and the lime juice, then season with salt.
Dip a rice paper sheet in warm water for 5–10 seconds, until just starting to soften. Lay it on a damp board.
Layer lettuce, vermicelli, carrot, cucumber, mint and coriander on the lower third, with 3 prawn halves on top. Fold in the bottom and sides, then roll up tightly.
Repeat to make 12 rolls, keeping them covered with a damp tea towel. Serve with the sauce.

batch_08.json::American Turkey Meatloaf.title: Turkey meatloaf
quick_steps: Cook the onion and carrot in the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Tip into a large bowl and cool for 10 minutes. Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan), line a tray, and soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 2 minutes.
Mix the turkey mince, egg, soaked breadcrumbs, salt and pepper into the cooled vegetables until just combined. Shape into a loose 22 cm loaf on the tray.
Whisk the tomato sauce, worcestershire sauce and brown sugar until smooth. Spread half over the loaf and bake for 35 minutes until lightly browned.
Spread on the remaining glaze and bake 15–20 minutes more, until sticky and 74°C in the centre, or the juices run clear with no pink.
Rest the loaf on the tray for 10 minutes, then cut into thick slices.

batch_08.json::Mexican Tostadas de Frijo.title: Tostadas de frijoles
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush the tortillas on both sides with half the olive oil and bake on lined trays for 8–10 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Cool the tortillas on the trays for 5 minutes so they crisp further.
Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4–5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cumin and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the pinto beans, salt and 80 ml water and simmer for 5 minutes until heated through. Mash roughly until thick and spreadable, then keep warm off the heat.
Shred the lettuce, dice the tomatoes, crumble the feta and cut one lime into wedges. Slice the avocado and squeeze the other lime over it.
Spread the beans over the tortillas, top with the lettuce, tomatoes, avocado and feta, and serve straight away with the lime wedges.

batch_08.json::Italian Ricotta Pancakes.title: Ricotta pancakes
quick_steps: Separate the eggs. Whisk the yolks with the ricotta, milk, half the sugar and the lemon zest until smooth, then stir in the sifted flour, baking powder and salt.
Whisk the egg whites for 2–3 minutes until soft peaks form. Fold them into the batter in three batches until no white streaks remain.
Heat the oven to 120°C (100°C fan) with a tray inside. Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat until foaming.
Cook about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake for 2–3 minutes each side, until golden and springy. Keep warm in the oven and repeat with the remaining butter and batter.
Simmer the blueberries, remaining sugar and 1 tbsp lemon juice in a small pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until softened and juicy.
Stack the pancakes and spoon the warm berries over to serve.

batch_08.json::Greek Yoghurt Honey Bowls.title: Greek yoghurt honey bowls
quick_steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Tip onto a plate to cool.
Finely grate the zest of the orange. Quarter the figs, and squeeze 1 tbsp orange juice if you want a looser drizzle.
Divide the Greek yoghurt among 4 bowls, then top with the fig quarters and cooled walnuts.
Drizzle 1 tbsp honey over each bowl, sprinkle with the cinnamon and orange zest, and serve straight away.

batch_08.json::Spanish Pan con Tomate.title: Pan con tomate
quick_steps: Halve the tomatoes and grate the cut sides into a bowl, discarding the skins. Stir in 1/4 tsp of the salt and leave to drain slightly.
Heat a chargrill pan or large frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes.
Toast the bread for 2–3 minutes per side, until golden with charred marks, crisp outside and slightly chewy inside.
Rub the garlic clove over one side of each hot slice so it grates into the bread.
Spoon the grated tomato over the garlic side, drizzle with the olive oil and sprinkle with the remaining salt. Serve straight away.

batch_08.json::Italian Marinated Articho.title: Marinated artichokes
quick_steps: Drain the artichoke hearts well and pat dry, then halve or quarter any large pieces. Place them in a medium bowl.
Zest the lemon and juice it to get about 2 tbsp. Stir the zest and juice with the chopped parsley and salt in a small bowl.
Heat the olive oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add the sliced garlic, oregano and chilli flakes and cook for 2 minutes, until fragrant but not browned.
Cool the oil for 5 minutes until warm, then stir it into the lemon mixture.
Pour the dressing over the artichokes and toss gently. Leave at room temperature for 30 minutes, tossing once halfway.
Serve at room temperature, spooning over the dressing from the bowl.

batch_08.json::Chinese Garlic Green Bean.title: Garlic green beans
quick_steps: Trim the green beans, halving any very long ones, then wash and dry them thoroughly. Finely chop the garlic and stir the soy sauce and sugar together in a small bowl.
Heat a wok over high heat for 1 minute, then add half the vegetable oil. Stir-fry half the beans for 3–4 minutes, until blistered and tender-crisp. Transfer to a plate.
Repeat with the remaining oil and beans, leaving them in the wok. Return the first batch and reduce the heat to medium.
Push the beans aside and stir the garlic in for 30 seconds, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the soy mixture and salt, then toss for 1 minute, until the beans are lightly glazed.
Remove from the heat, drizzle with the sesame oil, toss once and serve straight away.

batch_08.json::French Pear Tarte Tatin.title: Pear tarte tatin
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Peel, halve and core the pears, toss them in the juice of half the lemon, and cut the pastry into a round 2 cm wider than the pan, then prick it.
Sprinkle the sugar over a 24 cm ovenproof pan and heat on medium without stirring until deep amber, 6–8 minutes. Off the heat, swirl in the butter and vanilla.
Pack the pears cut-side up into the caramel. Cook on medium for 8–10 minutes, spooning caramel over, until bubbling, thick and the pears are slightly soft.
Lay the pastry over the pears and tuck in the edges. Bake for 25–30 minutes until puffed, deep golden and crisp.
Rest for 5 minutes, then run a knife around the edge and flip onto a large plate with oven mitts. Serve warm.

batch_08.json::Indian Kheer Rice Pudding.title: Kheer rice pudding
quick_steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then soak in cold water for 15 minutes and drain. Lightly crush the cardamom pods so they split open.
Heat the milk in a large heavy-based saucepan over medium heat until small bubbles form around the edge, about 8 minutes.
Add the rice, cardamom and saffron. Bring to a gentle simmer, about 5 minutes, then reduce the heat to low.
Cook on low for 35 minutes, stirring often and scraping the base, until the rice is very soft and the milk is thick and creamy.
Stir in the sugar and cook 5 more minutes, until dissolved and the kheer coats the back of a spoon.
Remove the cardamom pods and stir in the rosewater. Rest for 10 minutes, then serve warm topped with the chopped pistachios.

batch_08.json::Greek Tzatziki.title: Tzatziki
quick_steps: Coarsely grate the cucumber, skin on, and toss with 1/4 tsp of the salt. Leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze very dry in a clean tea towel.
Chop the garlic and crush it with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt until it forms a smooth paste.
Stir the Greek yoghurt until smooth in a medium bowl. Mix in the cucumber, garlic paste, dill and lemon juice until evenly combined.
Taste and add a little more lemon juice if you'd like it sharper.
Cover and chill for at least 20 minutes. Stir, then spoon into a serving bowl and drizzle with the olive oil just before serving.

batch_08.json::American Peach Cobbler.title: Peach cobbler
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Toss the peaches in a 1.5 litre baking dish with half the sugar, the lemon juice and cinnamon.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and remaining sugar in a large bowl. Rub in the cold butter until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in the milk with a fork until a soft, sticky dough forms and no dry flour remains.
Drop heaped spoonfuls of dough over the peaches, leaving small gaps. Bake for 35–40 minutes, until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Check the juices are bubbling thickly at the edges. Cover loosely with foil for the last 10 minutes if it browns too fast.
Rest for 10 minutes, then spoon into bowls with plenty of the juices.

batch_08.json::French Clafoutis with Che.title: Clafoutis with cherries
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease a 1.5 litre shallow dish with the softened butter and scatter the pitted cherries over the base in a single layer.
Whisk the eggs and caster sugar for 1–2 minutes until pale and slightly thickened. Whisk in the flour and salt, then the milk, melted butter and vanilla until smooth and thin like pouring cream.
Rest the batter for 5 minutes, then pour it slowly over the cherries.
Bake in the middle of the oven for 35–40 minutes, until puffed, golden and just set with a slight wobble in the centre.
Rest in the dish for 10–15 minutes. Dust with the icing sugar and serve warm or at room temperature in wedges.

batch_08.json::Vietnamese Caramelised Po.title: Vietnamese caramelised pork bowls
quick_steps: Finely chop the garlic and shallots, slice the cucumber and cut the lime into wedges.
Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook per the packet over low heat once boiling, until tender. Keep covered off the heat.

Heat the brown sugar with 1 tbsp water in a small saucepan over medium heat, without stirring, for 3–4 minutes until deep amber. Carefully add 3 tbsp warm water, stir over low heat until smooth, then add the fish sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork for 5–6 minutes until browned and no longer pink. Add the shallots and garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the caramel and black pepper and simmer over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until thick and glossy. Serve over the rice with the cucumber and lime.

stages.title: Prepare the aromatics and cucumber
steps: Finely chop the garlic and shallots and keep them together in a small bowl.
Slice the cucumber into thin rounds and cut the lime into wedges.
Measure the brown sugar into a small saucepan and measure the fish sauce into a small jug, ready to use.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the rice according to the packet, over low heat once boiling, until tender, then keep it covered off the heat until the pork is ready.

stages.title: Make the caramel
steps: Add 1 tbsp water to the brown sugar in the saucepan and heat over medium heat, without stirring, for 3–4 minutes until deep amber.
Stand back and carefully add 3 tbsp warm water, as the caramel will splutter. Stir over low heat for 1 minute until smooth, then stir in the fish sauce and remove from the heat.

stages.title: Cook the pork
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the pork mince and cook for 5–6 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and no longer pink.
Add the shallots and garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the caramel and add the black pepper. Simmer over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and glossy and clings to the pork.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Divide the rice among four bowls and spoon the pork and its sauce over the top.
Add the cucumber slices and a lime wedge to each bowl, and squeeze the lime over just before eating.

batch_08.json::Australian Anzac Biscuits.title: Anzac biscuits
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line two large trays with baking paper. Mix the oats, flour, coconut and brown sugar in a large bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup in a small saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes until smooth.
Stir the bicarbonate soda into the boiling water, add it to the pan (it will foam), then take the pan off the heat.
Pour the butter mixture into the dry mix and stir until it's evenly moistened and holds together when pressed.
Roll heaped tablespoons into about 20 balls, place them 5 cm apart on the trays and flatten to about 1 cm thick.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until deep golden brown at the edges. Cool on the trays for 10 minutes, then move to a wire rack.

batch_08.json::American Banana Cream Pie.title: Banana cream pie
quick_steps: Crush the biscuits to fine crumbs and mix with the butter, melted over low heat. Press into a 20 cm pie dish and chill for 30 minutes, until firm.
Heat the milk over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, until steaming with small bubbles at the edge. Don't let it boil.
Whisk the egg yolks, sugar and cornflour until pale and smooth, then slowly whisk in the hot milk.
Return to the pan over medium heat and stir for 4–5 minutes, until thick and bubbling, then 1 minute more. Off the heat, stir in the vanilla and cool under cling film for 10 minutes.
Layer 2 sliced bananas over the crust, pour over the custard and chill for at least 4 hours, until completely set.
Whip the cream to soft peaks (2–3 minutes) and swirl over the pie. Top with the remaining sliced banana just before serving.

batch_08.json::Greek Portokalopita.title: Portokalopita
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Tear the filo into 3–4 cm pieces and bake on a lined tray for 10–12 minutes until dry and crisp but not coloured, then cool for 20 minutes.
Grease and line a 20 cm tin with 1 tsp olive oil. Zest and juice 2 oranges, keeping the juice for the syrup.
Whisk the eggs and 100 g sugar for 2 minutes until pale and thick. Whisk in the yoghurt, 150 ml olive oil, zest, vanilla and baking powder until smooth.
Fold in the cooled filo until coated, then pour into the tin and level. Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 40–45 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Meanwhile, juice the last orange and simmer it with the reserved juice, remaining 150 g sugar and 200 ml water in a saucepan over medium heat for 8–10 minutes until lightly syrupy. Cool to warm.
Rest the cake in its tin for 10 minutes until warm, then slowly pour over the warm syrup. Leave for 30 minutes to soak, then cut into 4.

batch_08.json::Mexican Churros with Choc.title: Churros with chocolate sauce
quick_steps: Bring the water, butter and salt to the boil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour, reduce to low and stir 1–2 minutes, until the dough forms a smooth ball.
Cool the dough for 5 minutes. Beat in the eggs and vanilla in 3 additions until thick and glossy, then pipe 10–12 cm lengths onto a lined tray.
Put the chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Heat the cream in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until steaming, then pour over the chocolate and stir until smooth.
Mix the caster sugar and cinnamon on a plate. Heat the oil in a deep saucepan over medium heat to 175°C.
Fry 4 churros at a time for 3–4 minutes, until deep golden and cooked through. Drain briefly, roll in the cinnamon sugar and serve hot with the chocolate sauce.

batch_08.json::Italian Ribollita.title: Ribollita
quick_steps: Finely dice the onion, carrots and celery. Crush the garlic, pick the thyme leaves, slice the kale and tear the bread into 2 cm pieces.
Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots, celery and salt for 10 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute until fragrant.
Mash half the beans. Add them with the whole beans, tomatoes and stock, bring to the boil over high heat, then simmer over medium-low for 15 minutes until the vegetables are very tender.
Stir in the kale and simmer for 8 minutes until dark and tender.
Stir in the bread, take off the heat and rest 15 minutes until swollen and thick. Warm over low heat for 5 minutes until steaming.
Season with pepper and extra salt if needed. Drizzle each serving with the remaining olive oil.

batch_08.json::Thai Larb Gai.title: Larb gai
quick_steps: Toast the rice in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until deep golden, then cool and grind to a coarse powder.
Juice 2 limes and cut the third into wedges. Slice the shallots, pick the mint, chop the coriander, then stir the fish sauce into the juice.
Cook the chicken mince with 60 ml water in a large pan over medium-high heat for 7–8 minutes until cooked through, no longer pink and mostly dry.
Pour the fish sauce mixture over the warm mince and add the chilli flakes and shallots. Fold in the rice powder, mint and coriander, then adjust to taste.
Spoon into the lettuce leaves and serve with the lime wedges.

stages.title: Make the toasted rice powder
steps: Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat and add the 2 tbsp rice.
Toast, shaking the pan often, for 4–5 minutes until deep golden and fragrant.
Tip the rice onto a plate and cool for 3 minutes.
Grind the rice in a mortar or spice grinder to a coarse powder, like fine sand with some texture.

stages.title: Prepare the dressing and herbs
steps: Juice 2 of the limes to get about 80 ml juice and cut the remaining lime into wedges for serving.
Thinly slice the shallots and pick the mint leaves.
Roughly chop the coriander and separate the lettuce leaves, then keep them cold until serving.
Stir the fish sauce and lime juice together in a small bowl.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat and add the chicken mince with 60 ml water.
Cook for 7–8 minutes, breaking up the mince with a wooden spoon, until cooked through and no longer pink, and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Take the pan off the heat and let the mince cool for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Pour the fish sauce and lime mixture over the warm chicken and stir through the chilli flakes and shallots.
Fold in the ground toasted rice, mint and coriander.
Taste and add a little more fish sauce or lime if needed.
Spoon the larb into the lettuce leaves and serve with the lime wedges.

batch_08.json::Indian Baingan Bharta.title: Baingan bharta
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Prick the eggplants, rub with 1 tbsp of the oil and roast 35–40 minutes, turning once, until blackened and completely soft.
Rest the eggplants for 10 minutes, then scoop out the flesh, discarding the skins and any bitter liquid. Chop roughly until mashed but still a little chunky.
Heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the cumin seeds 30 seconds until fragrant, then the onion for 6–7 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli and cook 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, turmeric and salt and cook 6–8 minutes until a thick, jammy paste forms.
Stir in the eggplant and cook over medium-low heat for 8 minutes until thick and the oil separates at the edges. Stir through the coriander, taste for salt and serve hot.

batch_08.json::German Kartoffelsalat.title: Kartoffelsalat
quick_steps: Simmer the whole unpeeled potatoes in salted water, boiling on high then medium, for 20–25 minutes until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Drain, cool for about 5 minutes, then peel and slice the potatoes 5 mm thick into a large bowl.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the bacon for 5–6 minutes until golden and crisp, then add the onion and cook 3–4 minutes until soft.
Add the stock, vinegar, mustard and sugar, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced, then add the salt and pepper.
Pour the hot dressing over the warm potatoes and fold gently. Rest for 15–20 minutes, folding once, until most of the liquid is absorbed.
Taste, adjust with salt or vinegar, then fold through the parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

batch_08.json::Peruvian Aji de Gallina.title: Aji de gallina
quick_steps: Simmer the chicken breast in the stock and 400 ml water over medium heat, then low for 15–18 minutes, until cooked through and no longer pink. Rest 10 minutes, shred, and keep the broth.
Soak the bread in the evaporated milk for 5 minutes, then blend with the walnuts, parmesan and 250 ml warm broth until completely smooth.
Cook the onion and salt in the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat for 5–6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, aji amarillo paste and turmeric for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Pour in the blended sauce and simmer over low heat for 8–10 minutes, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Loosen with a splash of broth if needed.
Cook the rice to packet directions. Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, until the yolks are firm, then cool, peel and quarter.
Warm the shredded chicken in the sauce over low heat for 3–4 minutes, until hot through, and season with black pepper. Serve over the rice with the eggs and kalamata olives.

batch_08.json::Egyptian Ful Medames.title: Ful medames
quick_steps: Chop the tomatoes and parsley. Crush the garlic with the salt into a paste, and juice the lemons (about 80 ml).
Tip both cans of fava beans with their liquid into a saucepan with 100 ml water. Simmer over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, until hot and slightly reduced.
Stir in the cumin and pepper for 1 minute. Reduce to low and mash about half the beans, leaving the rest whole.
Stir in the garlic paste, 1 tbsp olive oil and two-thirds of the lemon juice. Simmer 3–4 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Warm the pita in a dry frying pan over medium heat, about 1 minute each side, until soft and lightly toasted.
Divide the beans among bowls. Top with the tomatoes, parsley and chilli flakes, drizzle with the remaining oil and lemon juice, and serve with the pita.

batch_08.json::French Madeleines.title: Madeleines
quick_steps: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes until liquid, then cool to lukewarm. Sift the flour and baking powder together and grate the lemon zest.
Beat the eggs and caster sugar on high for 5–6 minutes until pale, thick and doubled. Whisk in the vanilla and zest, then fold in the flour mixture and cooled butter until smooth and glossy.
Cover and chill the batter for 45 minutes until firm enough to hold its shape. Meanwhile, brush the tin with the softened extra butter, dust with the extra flour and chill it.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the batter into the moulds, about three-quarters full, and bake for 9–11 minutes until risen, golden at the edges and springy.
Tip the madeleines onto a wire rack and cool for 10 minutes. Dust with the icing sugar and serve slightly warm.

batch_08.json::Greek Gemista Stuffed Tom.title: Gemista (stuffed tomatoes)
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Slice the tops off the tomatoes and capsicums, deseed the capsicums, and scoop the tomato flesh into a bowl, leaving a 1 cm shell. Chop the pulp.
Stand the shells snugly in a baking dish. Cook the onion in 2 tbsp olive oil in a pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, until soft.

Add the garlic and pine nuts and cook for 1 minute until golden. Stir in the rice, tomato pulp and juices, salt and pepper, and cook 2–3 minutes until bubbling. Stir through the parsley and mint off the heat.
Fill the shells until three-quarters full and replace the tops. Pour the stock around the vegetables and drizzle with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.
Cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes until the vegetables soften. Uncover and bake 15 minutes more, until the tops are browned and the rice is tender.
Rest for 10 minutes, then serve with the pan juices spooned over.

batch_08.json::French Leek and Potato So.title: Leek and potato soup
quick_steps: Rinse and thinly slice the leeks, cube the potatoes into 2 cm pieces and snip the chives.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over low-medium heat. Add the leeks and salt, cover and cook 10–12 minutes until soft and silky, not browned.
Add the potatoes and stock, bring to the boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to low-medium and partly cover. Simmer 18–20 minutes until the potato breaks apart easily.
Cool for 5 minutes, then blend until completely smooth.
Return to the pan over low heat and stir in the cream, nutmeg and pepper. Warm gently for 2–3 minutes without boiling, then adjust the salt.
Ladle into bowls and scatter with the chives.

batch_08.json::Mexican Sopa de Fideo.title: Sopa de fideo
quick_steps: Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic and 250 ml of the stock for 1 minute until completely smooth. Break the vermicelli into 4–5 cm lengths.
Heat the oil in a large deep saucepan over medium heat. Cook the vermicelli for 3–5 minutes until evenly deep golden, not dark brown.
Pour in the blended tomato mixture, standing back as it spits. Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes until darker and slightly thickened, then add the salt and pepper.
Add the remaining 750 ml stock, scraping up the base. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium-low.
Simmer for 5–7 minutes until the noodles are tender and the soup has thickened slightly. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Ladle into four bowls, scatter over the coriander and serve with the lime wedges.

batch_09.json::Japanese Oyakodon.title: Oyakodon
quick_steps: Cook the rice according to the packet and keep it covered and warm. Cut the chicken into 2 cm pieces, slice the onion and spring onions, and lightly beat the eggs.
Combine the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a wide, deep frying pan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat until the sugar dissolves, about 2 minutes.
Add the onion and simmer for 5–6 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Add the chicken in a single layer and simmer for 8–9 minutes, turning once, until cooked through and no longer pink in the middle.
Pour the eggs over in a circle, then cover and cook over medium-low heat for 1–2 minutes, until the whites are just set and the yolks soft.
Spoon the chicken and egg with some pan juices over the rice in four bowls. Scatter with spring onions and serve.

batch_09.json::Thai Tom Kha Gai.title: Tom kha gai
quick_steps: Slice the chicken thinly. Bruise and cut the lemongrass, slice the ginger, tear the lime leaves, halve the mushrooms and slice the chillies.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Fry the lemongrass, ginger and lime leaves for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the stock and bring to a simmer, then reduce to low and simmer for 10 minutes. Stir in the coconut milk.
Add the chicken and mushrooms and simmer gently for 10–12 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink. Don't let it boil hard.
Off the heat, stir in the fish sauce and the juice of 1 lime. Taste and adjust.
Ladle into bowls and top with the chilli and coriander. Serve with the lime wedges and leave the lemongrass, ginger and lime leaves uneaten.

batch_09.json::Japanese Chicken Karaage.title: Chicken karaage
quick_steps: Trim the chicken thigh and cut into 4 cm chunks. Pat dry with paper towel.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, ginger and garlic in a bowl, add the chicken and toss to coat. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Lift the chicken from the marinade, discarding the rest, and press each piece into the cornflour until thickly coated. Shake off the excess.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat to 170°C, or until a pinch of cornflour sizzles steadily.
Fry the chicken in three batches for 5–6 minutes each, until deep golden and cooked through with no pink in the centre. Drain on a wire rack, reheating the oil to 170°C between batches.
Sprinkle the hot chicken with the salt and serve straight away with the lemon wedges.

batch_08.json::Italian Caprese Stuffed P.title: Caprese stuffed peppers
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the seeded capsicum halves cut side up on a lined tray, brush with half the olive oil and season with half the salt.
Roast for 20 minutes, until the edges start to colour and the flesh softens slightly.
Meanwhile, mix the cherry tomatoes, garlic, remaining oil and salt, pepper and half the basil. Tip any pooled liquid from the capsicums, then spoon in the filling.
Top with the torn mozzarella and bake at 200°C for 10–12 minutes, until the cheese is melted and lightly golden and the capsicums are tender.
Meanwhile, simmer the balsamic vinegar in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until syrupy.
Rest the capsicums for 3 minutes, then drizzle with the balsamic syrup and top with the remaining basil.

batch_09.json::French Pommes Dauphinoise.title: Pommes dauphinoise
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Grease a 20 x 25 cm dish with half the butter, then peel and slice the potatoes 2–3 mm thick, without rinsing.
Warm the cream, milk, garlic, thyme, nutmeg, salt and pepper in a saucepan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until steaming and just bubbling at the edges. Don't boil.
Layer the potatoes and cream mixture in the dish in three rounds, finishing with cream. Press down and cover tightly with foil.
Bake covered for 50 minutes, until the potatoes are nearly tender when pierced.
Uncover, dot with the remaining butter and bake 25 minutes more, until deep golden and a knife slides in easily.
Rest for 15 minutes to let the sauce thicken, then cut and serve hot.

batch_09.json::British Toad in the Hole.title: Toad in the hole
quick_steps: Whisk 140 g of the plain flour, 1/4 tsp salt, eggs, milk, 100 ml water and black pepper into a smooth batter like pouring cream. Rest it for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Roast the sausages in the vegetable oil in a metal baking dish for 12 minutes until browned, then 3 minutes more until the oil is smoking hot.
Pour the batter around the sausages and bake for 25–30 minutes, until risen and deep golden and the sausages are cooked through with no pink.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onions with the remaining salt for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the remaining 1 tbsp flour for 1 minute, then add the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer 8–10 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon.
Cut the pudding into four portions with two sausages each and serve straight away with the gravy.

batch_09.json::Mexican Esquites.title: Esquites
quick_steps: Pat the corn very dry. Zest and juice the lime, crumble the feta and chop the coriander. Mix the mayonnaise, lime zest, half the juice and half the chilli powder in a large bowl.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over high heat until foaming. Add the corn in a single layer and cook 3 minutes without stirring, until browned underneath.
Stir, then cook 4–5 minutes more, stirring only occasionally, until charred in spots and lightly popping. Stir in the salt and remaining lime juice, then take off the heat.
Toss the hot corn through the mayonnaise mixture until coated. Spoon into 4 bowls and top with the feta, coriander and remaining chilli powder. Serve warm.

batch_09.json::Indian Dal Tadka.title: Dal tadka
quick_steps: Rinse the moong dal until the water runs almost clear. Chop the onion, tomatoes and coriander, and slice the garlic.
Bring the dal, turmeric, half the onion, tomatoes and 1 litre water to the boil in a large saucepan over high heat. Simmer partly covered on medium-low for 30 minutes, until very soft.
About 15 minutes before the dal is ready, cook the rice to packet directions and keep it covered and warm.
Stir the salt into the dal, adding a splash of hot water if it is thicker than pourable soup.

Heat the ghee in a small frying pan over medium heat. Cook the cumin seeds until they sizzle, then the remaining onion until lightly browned. Add the garlic and dried chillies for 1 minute, until the garlic is golden.
Pour the hot tadka over the dal. Serve over the rice with the coriander and lemon wedges.

batch_09.json::Thai Mango Salad.title: Thai mango salad
quick_steps: Toast the peanuts in a small frying pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until golden and fragrant. Cool briefly, then roughly chop.
Peel the green mangoes and carrot and cut into thin matchsticks. Thinly slice the shallot and red chilli, and pick the coriander leaves.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice and brown sugar for about 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves. Adjust with more sugar or lime juice to taste.
Toss the mango, carrot, shallot and chilli with the dressing for about 1 minute. Leave to stand for 5 minutes, until the mango softens slightly.
Gently toss through the coriander, then plate and scatter with the peanuts. Serve straight away.

batch_09.json::Greek Revithia.title: Revithia
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Slice the onions and garlic, and zest and juice the lemon.
Heat half the olive oil in an ovenproof casserole over medium heat. Cook the onions with the salt for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, rosemary and bay leaf and cook 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chickpeas, stock, pepper and remaining oil. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, cover and bake 50 minutes until the chickpeas are very tender.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes more until lightly browned and glossy. Remove the rosemary and bay leaf.
Stir in the lemon juice and most of the zest, and season to taste. Rest 5 minutes, then serve with bread and the remaining zest.

batch_08.json::Chinese Tomato Egg Stir-F.title: Tomato egg stir-fry
quick_steps: Cook the rice in a pan over low heat per the packet until tender, then keep it covered and warm.
Beat the eggs with half the salt. Cut the tomatoes into wedges, slice the spring onions (whites and greens apart), and mix the cornflour with 1 tbsp water.
Heat half the oil in a wok over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Scramble the eggs for 1–2 minutes until just set but still soft, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil and fry the spring onion whites for 20 seconds until fragrant. Add the tomatoes and remaining salt and cook 3–4 minutes until softened and juicy.
Stir in the sugar and soy sauce for 1 minute, then the cornflour mixture for 30 seconds until glossy.
Fold the eggs back through for 1 minute until cooked through, then top with the spring onion greens and serve with the rice.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Cook the rice in a pan over low heat according to the packet until tender, so it is ready when the stir-fry is finished.
While the rice cooks, beat the eggs in a bowl with 1/4 tsp of the salt until the whites and yolks are fully combined.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges and slice the spring onions, keeping the white and green parts separate.

stages.title: Prepare the sauce
steps: Mix the cornflour with 1 tbsp water in a small bowl until smooth.
Measure the sugar and soy sauce into a small bowl so they are ready to add.
Keep the rice covered and warm once cooked.

stages.title: Scramble the eggs
steps: Heat half the oil in a wok over medium-high heat for 1 minute until it shimmers.
Pour in the eggs and leave for 10 seconds, then gently push them from the edges to the centre.
Cook for 1–2 minutes until the eggs are just set but still soft and slightly wet in places, then transfer to a plate.

stages.title: Cook the tomatoes
steps: Add the remaining oil to the wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the spring onion whites for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and cook, stirring often, for 3–4 minutes until they soften and release their juices.
Stir in the sugar and soy sauce and cook for 1 minute.
Stir the cornflour mixture, pour it in and cook for 30 seconds until the sauce thickens slightly and turns glossy.

stages.title: Combine and serve
steps: Return the eggs to the wok and fold gently through the tomatoes for 1 minute until the eggs are cooked through and no longer wet.
Scatter over the spring onion greens and serve straight away with the rice.

batch_09_part_2.json::French Salade Niço.title: Salade niçoise
quick_steps: Boil the eggs in a saucepan over high heat, then medium-high, for 9 minutes until the yolks are firm. Cool in iced water, then peel and quarter.
Blanch the green beans in salted boiling water over high heat for 3–4 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Cool in cold water, then drain and dry.
Whisk the dijon mustard, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a bowl, then whisk in the olive oil until thick and emulsified.
Spread the lettuce on a large platter. Arrange the beans, cherry tomatoes, olives and tuna in groups on top.
Add the egg quarters and drizzle with the dressing just before serving.

batch_09.json::Italian Semifreddo.title: Semifreddo
quick_steps: Line a 1 litre loaf tin with baking paper, leaving an overhang to lift it out. Roughly chop the toasted hazelnuts.
Whisk the eggs, caster sugar and salt in a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of simmering water on low heat. Keep going for 6–8 minutes, until pale, thick and 71°C.
Beat the egg mixture with electric beaters on high for 5–6 minutes, until thick, glossy and completely cool.
Whip the thickened cream to soft peaks. Stir the vanilla extract into the egg mixture, fold it into the cream in two batches, then fold in the hazelnuts.
Pour into the tin, smooth the top, cover with the paper overhang and freeze for at least 6 hours, until firm all the way through.
Lift out and stand for 5 minutes to soften slightly. Slice with a knife dipped in hot water and serve straight away.

batch_09.json::Mexican Sopa de Tortilla.title: Sopa de tortilla
quick_steps: Soak the seeded ancho chilli in 250 ml boiling water for 15 minutes, until soft. Meanwhile, cut the corn tortillas into 1 cm strips.
Blend the chilli with 2 tbsp of its soaking water, the canned tomatoes, onion and garlic for 1 minute, until smooth.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Carefully add the puree and cook for 5 minutes until darkened and fragrant, then add the cumin and salt for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken stock and bring to a simmer, then reduce to low and simmer for 30 minutes, until slightly thickened.
While it simmers, toss the tortilla strips with the vegetable oil and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 8–10 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Taste and add more salt if needed. Ladle into bowls and top with the tortilla strips, avocado and coriander, with lime wedges to serve.

batch_09_part_2.json::Italian Zuppa Tosc.title: Zuppa Toscana
quick_steps: Squeeze the sausages from their casings. Finely chop the onion and garlic, slice the potatoes 5 mm thick and tear the kale.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Cook the sausage meat for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and no longer pink.
Reduce to medium and cook the onion for 3–4 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the potatoes, stock and water, scraping up the browned bits. Boil on high, then simmer partly covered on medium-low for 12–15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Stir in the kale and simmer for 4–5 minutes until wilted. Add the cream and warm for 2–3 minutes until steaming, without boiling.
Season with the salt and pepper, taste and adjust, then serve hot.

batch_09_part_2.json::Lebanese Batata Ha.title: Batata harra
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) with a large baking tray inside. Cut the potatoes into 2 cm cubes, then chop the garlic and coriander and halve the lemon.
Cover the potatoes with cold water, add 1 tsp of the salt and bring to the boil on high. Reduce to medium and simmer 6–8 minutes, until the edges are soft but the cubes hold their shape.
Drain well and steam dry for 3 minutes, shaking to roughen the edges. Toss with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Tip onto the hot tray in a single layer and roast 20 minutes. Turn and roast another 12–15 minutes, until deep golden and crisp outside and tender inside.
Warm the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil in a small pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Cook the garlic and chilli flakes for 30–60 seconds, until fragrant and pale golden, then take off the heat.
Toss the hot potatoes with the garlic and chilli oil, coriander and lemon juice. Serve straight away, with chilli oil if you like.

batch_09_part_2.json::Chinese Egg Drop S.title: Egg drop soup
quick_steps: Slice the ginger and spring onions, keeping the spring onions separate. Beat the eggs in a jug, and mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Put the stock, 250 ml water and ginger in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then simmer gently on medium-low for 8 minutes.
Remove the ginger, then season with the pepper and salt.
Return to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Stir in the cornflour mixture and cook for 1 minute until glossy and slightly thickened.
Reduce to low and swirl the soup. Pour in the eggs in a thin stream, then leave for 30 seconds until the ribbons are set and opaque.
Off the heat, stir in the sesame oil and most of the spring onions. Ladle into bowls and top with the rest.

batch_09_part_2.json::Moroccan Briouats.title: Moroccan briouats with almonds
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Mix the ground almonds, icing sugar, cinnamon, orange blossom water and 1 tbsp water into a firm, moist paste.
Cut the filo sheets lengthwise into 3 strips each, keeping them covered. Brush each strip with some of the melted butter and put 1 heaped teaspoon of paste at one end.
Fold each strip over the filling into a triangle, flag-style, to the end. Seal the loose end with butter and place seam-side down on a lined tray.
Brush the tops with the remaining butter. Bake for 15–18 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
Warm the honey with 1 tbsp water in a small saucepan over low heat for 2 minutes, until runny. Dip the warm triangles, then drain on a rack for 5 minutes, until tacky.

batch_09_part_2.json::Mexican Chilaquile.title: Chilaquiles verdes
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the tortilla triangles with 1 tbsp of the olive oil on two lined trays and bake for 12–15 minutes, until golden and crisp. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt.

Put the tomatillos, jalapeno, roughly chopped onion, garlic and coriander stems in a saucepan with 250 ml water. Bring to the boil over high heat, then simmer on medium-low for 10 minutes, until soft and dull olive green.
Blend the lot with the cooking liquid until smooth, then season with the remaining salt.

Simmer the sauce in a large frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened. Toss through the tortillas for 1 minute, until coated but still partly crisp, then divide among 4 plates.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks runny. Top each plate with an egg.
Scatter over the finely diced onion and coriander leaves, then spoon over the sour cream and serve.

batch_09_part_2.json::Japanese Hiyayakko.title: Hiyayakko
quick_steps: Refrigerate the silken tofu in its packet for at least 30 minutes until very cold, and chill four small plates alongside it.
Grate the ginger finely and lightly squeeze it, keeping the pulp and juice. Thinly slice the spring onions.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, until light golden and fragrant, then cool on a plate.
Tip the tofu onto paper towel, blot dry and cut into four even pieces. Slide each onto a chilled plate.
Top each piece with the ginger and spring onions, scatter over the sesame seeds and drizzle with the soy sauce. Serve straight away while cold.

batch_09_part_2.json::Irish Colcannon.title: Colcannon
quick_steps: Boil the potato chunks in salted water, bringing to the boil on high then simmering on medium for 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain and steam dry for 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, melt 20 g of the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the cabbage with 1/2 tsp of the salt for 5–6 minutes, until wilted but still bright green.
Add the spring onions, cook for 1 minute, then take the pan off the heat.
Warm the milk in a small saucepan over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until steaming but not boiling.
Mash the potatoes with the remaining 50 g butter until smooth. Stir in the warm milk, pepper and remaining salt until creamy, then fold through the cabbage mixture.
Spoon into a warm bowl, make a well in the centre and melt a knob of extra butter in it.

batch_09_part_2.json::Brazilian Pao de Q.title: Pão de queijo (cheese bread)
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush a 12-hole mini muffin tin with 1 tsp of the oil and tip the tapioca starch into a large heatproof bowl.
Heat the milk, remaining oil and salt in a small saucepan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until steaming with small bubbles at the edge. Don't let it boil hard.
Pour the hot liquid over the starch and mix until no dry patches remain and it looks shaggy and slightly translucent. Cool for about 10 minutes, until warm to the touch.
Beat in the egg for 2–3 minutes until the dough is smooth and very sticky, then mix in the parmesan until stretchy.
With wet hands, roll the dough into 12 golf-ball-sized balls and place one in each muffin hole.
Bake on the middle shelf for 20–22 minutes, until puffed, deep golden and set. Rest in the tin for 3 minutes, then serve warm.

batch_09_part_2.json::Italian Pasta e Ce.title: Pasta e ceci
quick_steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, setting aside 1/2 cup for garnish. Finely chop the onion and garlic, and chop the rosemary leaves.
Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and salt for 8–10 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and rosemary for 1 minute.
Add the passata, remaining chickpeas and stock, then boil on high. Simmer on medium-low, partly covered, for 15 minutes until the chickpeas are very tender.
Blend about 2 cups of chickpeas with some liquid until smooth, then stir back into the pot.
Simmer on medium, add the pasta and cook 8–10 minutes until al dente and thick. Season with pepper and extra salt, then rest off the heat for 2 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and top with the reserved chickpeas, remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the parmesan, if using.

batch_08.json::Japanese Chicken Soboro D.title: Chicken soboro don
quick_steps: Rinse the short-grain rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain. Cook on the stovetop over medium heat as the packet directs, then rest covered off the heat for 10 minutes and fluff.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin and sugar until dissolved. Beat the eggs with the salt until no white streaks remain. Grate the ginger and slice the spring onions.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the chicken mince and ginger for 3–4 minutes until no pink remains.
Add the soy mixture and cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until almost dry and the mince is glossy and cooked through. Tip into a bowl and keep warm.
Wipe the pan and scramble the eggs over low heat for 3–4 minutes until in small, soft curds and cooked through. Remove from the heat straight away.
Divide the rice among four bowls, topping each with chicken and egg. Scatter over the spring onions and serve warm.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse the short-grain rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Cook the rice according to the packet, using short-grain or sushi rice if you can.
Rest the rice, covered and off the heat, for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Grate the ginger and thinly slice the spring onions.
In a small bowl, mix the soy sauce, mirin and white sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Crack the eggs into a separate bowl, add the salt and beat until no streaks of white remain.

stages.title: Cook the chicken soboro
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the chicken mince and ginger, breaking the mince up with a wooden spoon or two spoons as it cooks, for 3–4 minutes until no pink remains.
Pour in the soy mixture and cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring constantly, until the liquid has almost evaporated and the mince is fine, glossy and cooked through.
Tip the chicken into a bowl and cover to keep warm.

stages.title: Scramble the eggs
steps: Wipe out the pan and place it over low heat.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir constantly with a spatula or chopsticks for 3–4 minutes until the eggs form small, soft curds and are cooked through with no liquid egg remaining.
Remove the pan from the heat straight away so the eggs do not turn dry.

stages.title: Assemble the bowls
steps: Divide the rice among four bowls.
Arrange the chicken on one half of each bowl and the egg on the other half.
Scatter the spring onions over the top and serve while warm.

batch_09_part_2.json::French Gougeres.title: Gougères
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two trays with baking paper. Grate the gruyere, reserving 2 tbsp for the top, and sift the flour.
Bring the water, milk, butter and salt to a rolling boil in a saucepan over medium heat. Off the heat, beat in the flour until smooth and the paste leaves the sides of the pan.
Cook the paste over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until a thin film forms on the base. Cool in a bowl for 5 minutes, until warm.
Beat in the whisked eggs in 3 batches until glossy and the paste falls in a thick ribbon. Stir in the gruyere, nutmeg and black pepper.
Pipe or spoon walnut-sized mounds onto the trays, 4 cm apart. Sprinkle with the reserved cheese, bake 10 minutes, then at 180°C (160°C fan) for 15–20 minutes, until puffed and deep golden.
Pierce each gougère with a skewer, then dry out in the switched-off oven for 5 minutes. Serve warm.

batch_09_part_2.json::Italian Sbrisolona.title: Sbrisolona
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Grease a 24 cm springform tin with a little extra butter and line the base with baking paper.
Combine the flour, polenta, almonds, sugar, lemon zest and salt in a large bowl.
Rub in the cold butter until you have coarse, uneven crumbs with some pea-sized lumps.
Toss through the egg yolks with a fork until the mixture clumps in places but stays crumbly. Don't knead it smooth.
Scatter the crumbs loosely into the tin and press very lightly, keeping the surface rough. Bake in the centre for 35–40 minutes, until deep golden with lightly browned edges and a dry, set centre.
Cool in the tin for 30 minutes, then remove the side and break into rustic pieces.

batch_09_part_2.json::Mexican Nopales Sa.title: Nopales salad
quick_steps: Rinse the nopales. Finely chop the tomatoes, red onion and coriander, then juice the limes. Put the tomato and onion in a large bowl.
Boil 2 litres water with 1 tbsp salt in a large saucepan over high heat. Add the nopales, reduce to medium and simmer 12–15 minutes, until tender but slightly firm and bright olive green.
Drain, rinse under cold water until no longer slippery, then pat dry. Spread on a tray for 15 minutes, until completely cool.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt, black pepper and half the coriander. Toss through the nopales, tomato and onion.
Cover and chill for 15 minutes. Scatter over the remaining coriander and serve cold.

batch_09_part_2.json::Korean Hobak Jeon.title: Hobak jeon
quick_steps: Lay the zucchini rounds on paper towel, sprinkle with the salt and leave for 10 minutes. Pat both sides dry.
Spread the flour in one shallow dish and beat the eggs in another.
Stir the soy sauce and rice vinegar together in a small bowl for the dipping sauce.
Heat some of the vegetable oil in a large non-stick frypan over medium heat. Dip each round in the flour, then the egg.
Fry in batches in a single layer for 2–3 minutes per side, until golden and the egg is set. Wipe the pan and add more oil before each batch.
Serve the jeon warm with the dipping sauce.

batch_09_part_2.json::Spanish Crema Cata.title: Crema catalana
quick_steps: Heat the milk, cinnamon stick, and lemon and orange peel in a saucepan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until steaming. Steep for 10 minutes, then strain.
Whisk the egg yolks, 60 g of the caster sugar and the cornflour until pale and smooth. Slowly whisk in the warm milk.
Return to the clean pan over low heat. Stir for 6–8 minutes until thick and coating a spoon, then bubble gently for 1 minute.
Divide among four 150 ml ramekins. Cool for 20 minutes, cover the surfaces with plastic wrap, then chill for at least 3 hours until firm.
Blot the surfaces dry and sprinkle with the remaining 30 g sugar. Torch for 1–2 minutes per custard until deep golden, then rest 2 minutes to harden.

batch_09_part_2.json::Greek Skordalia.title: Skordalia
quick_steps: Peel and cut the potatoes into 3 cm chunks, then cover with cold water in a saucepan and add half the salt.
Pound the garlic with the remaining salt into a smooth, sticky paste with no visible pieces. Juice the lemon.
Bring the potatoes to the boil over high heat, then simmer on medium for 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Drain, then leave the potatoes in the dry hot pan off the heat for 2 minutes to steam dry.
Mash until completely smooth, then mix in the garlic paste. Beat in the olive oil bit by bit until thick, creamy and glossy.
Stir in the lemon juice and adjust the salt, then serve warm or at room temperature with a drizzle of extra oil.

batch_09_part_2.json::Vietnamese Che Ba.title: Chè ba màu (three-colour dessert)
quick_steps: Simmer the red beans with 3 tbsp of the sugar and 100 ml water in a small saucepan over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes, until syrupy and glossy. Cool in a bowl.
Cook the mung beans the same way with 3 tbsp of the sugar and 100 ml water, keeping them whole, until the liquid thickens and coats them. Cool in a bowl.
Whisk the cornflour with 2 tbsp water, then add the coconut milk, remaining sugar and salt. Heat over medium for 3–4 minutes until slightly thickened, without boiling hard, then cool for 5 minutes.
Cover and chill the beans and coconut sauce for at least 20 minutes, until cold. Keep the pandan jelly strips in the fridge.
Layer the mung beans, red beans and pandan jelly in 4 tall glasses, pack in the crushed ice, then pour over the cold sauce and serve straight away.

batch_09_part_2.json::Peruvian Causa Lim.title: Causa limeña
quick_steps: Boil the potatoes with half the salt over high heat, then simmer on medium for 15–18 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain and steam dry for 3 minutes.
Mash the warm potatoes until smooth. Mix in the juice of 2 limes, aji amarillo paste, olive oil and remaining salt, then knead until it holds together like soft dough.
Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, spring onions, juice of the last lime and black pepper in a bowl until creamy.
Line a 20 cm square dish or four 9 cm ring moulds with baking paper or plastic wrap. Press in half the potato, then top with the tuna filling and avocado slices.
Press the remaining potato over the top and smooth it. Refrigerate for at least 45 minutes until firm and cold.
Lift out, cut into 4 portions with a clean sharp knife and serve cold.

batch_09_part_2.json::Japanese Chawanmus.title: Chawanmushi
quick_steps: Gently whisk the eggs, then stir in the cooled dashi, soy sauce and mirin. Strain through a fine sieve into a clean jug.
Heat the oil in a small frying pan over medium heat. Cook the shiitake for 2–3 minutes until softened and lightly golden, then cool briefly.
Divide the mushrooms and prawns among four 200 ml heatproof cups, pour in the strained custard and skim off any bubbles.
Cover each cup tightly with foil. Bring 2 cm of water to the boil in a lidded pan or wok with a rack, then reduce to low.
Steam the cups with the lid slightly ajar for 15–20 minutes, until just set with a slight wobble and the juices run clear.
Rest the cups for 3 minutes, scatter over the spring onion and serve warm.

batch_09_part_2.json::Indian Sabudana Kh.title: Sabudana khichdi
quick_steps: Rinse the sabudana pearls until the water runs almost clear, then soak in 200 ml water for 4 hours until soft. Drain and rest for 15 minutes.
Dice the potato, chop the chilli and coriander, and crush the peanuts. Toss the pearls with the peanuts and salt.
Heat the ghee in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Fry the cumin seeds for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the potato and cook for 8–10 minutes until golden and tender. Stir in the chilli and cook for 1 minute.
Reduce to medium-low, add the pearl mixture and cook for 5–7 minutes until translucent and soft through.
Off the heat, stir in the lime juice and check the salt. Scatter with coriander and serve warm.

batch_09_part_2.json::French Socca.title: Socca
quick_steps: Whisk the chickpea flour, salt, 300 ml water and 1 tbsp olive oil into a smooth batter. Rest for 30 minutes, then skim off any foam.
While it rests, heat a 28 cm cast-iron pan in the oven at 250°C (230°C fan) for at least 5 minutes, until very hot. Turn the grill on high if you have one.
Carefully remove the pan and swirl in 1 tbsp olive oil. Pour in the batter straight away to make a layer about 3 mm thick.
Bake for 6–8 minutes, until the edges are crisp and the top is blistered, firm and golden in patches.
Brush with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and sprinkle with the black pepper. Cut into wedges and serve hot.

batch_09_part_2.json::Moroccan Baghrir.title: Baghrir
quick_steps: Blend the semolina, flour, yeast, baking powder, salt and warm water for 2 minutes until smooth and like thin pouring cream. Pour into a jug.
Cover and rest in a warm spot for 30 minutes, until foamy and bubbly. Stir gently once.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe with a thin film of oil. Pour in about 80 ml batter and swirl into a 12 cm round.
Cook one side only for 2–3 minutes, until covered in small holes and no longer wet or shiny. Don't flip. Cool on a tea towel, holes up, and repeat for about 12.
Melt the butter and honey in a small saucepan over low heat for 2 minutes until runny. Drizzle over the pancakes and serve.

batch_09_part_2.json::Portuguese Bifana.title: Bifana
quick_steps: Pound the pork slices to about 3 mm thick between baking paper. Crush the garlic with a pinch of the salt into a paste.
Mix the garlic paste with the remaining salt, pepper, paprika, bay leaves, white wine and 1 tbsp olive oil. Add the pork, coat and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Lift out the pork, keeping the marinade, and pat dry. Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat and sear the pork in 2 batches, 1 minute per side until browned.
Pour the marinade and bay leaves into the pan and simmer over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until reduced by half. Return the pork and simmer 2 minutes until cooked through with no pink remaining.
Warm the bread rolls in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 3–4 minutes until crisp outside and soft inside. Discard the bay leaves, then fill the rolls with pork and spoon over the sauce.

batch_09_part_2.json::Chinese Sesame Bal.title: Sesame balls
quick_steps: Dissolve the sugar in the warm water, then mix it gradually into the glutinous rice flour. Knead 2–3 minutes until smooth and soft, then cover with a damp tea towel.
Roll the red bean paste into 16 small balls of about 10 g. Divide the dough into 16 pieces of about 25 g and flatten each into a disc.
Wrap each disc around a ball of bean paste and pinch to seal. Roll smooth, moisten lightly, then coat evenly in the sesame seeds.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pan over medium-low heat to 150–160°C, until a sesame seed sizzles gently without browning.
Fry 5–6 balls at a time for 6–8 minutes, turning, until puffed, floating and golden. Drain, and bring the oil back to temperature between batches.
Rest for 5 minutes, as the filling is very hot. Serve warm while the shells are crisp.

batch_09_part_2.json::Italian Frittata d.title: Frittata di zucchine
quick_steps: Whisk the eggs with the parmesan, salt, pepper and half the torn basil. Thinly slice the zucchini into 3 mm rounds and the onion.
Heat the olive oil in a 24 cm ovenproof non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the zucchini and cook for 8 minutes until golden at the edges and the moisture has evaporated.
Heat the grill to high. Spread the vegetables over the pan, reduce to medium-low, pour in the egg mixture and cook for 5 minutes until the edges are set and the centre is still slightly wet.
Grill for 2–3 minutes until the top is golden and the centre no longer wobbles.
Rest in the pan for 3 minutes, scatter over the remaining basil and cut into 4 wedges.

batch_09_part_2.json::American Devilled.title: Devilled eggs
quick_steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water in a saucepan over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 10 minutes, until the yolks are cooked through and pale yellow.
Chill the eggs in ice water for 15 minutes, until completely cold. Peel under cold running water and pat dry.
Halve the eggs lengthways. Mash the yolks until fine and crumbly, then stir in the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper until smooth and creamy.
Spoon or pipe the filling into the whites. Refrigerate for 10 minutes to firm up.
Dust with the paprika, scatter over the chives and serve.

batch_09_part_2.json::Greek Fasolakia La.title: Fasolakia lathera
quick_steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the grated tomato, oregano, salt and pepper, and simmer 3–4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the potatoes and green beans, coat in the sauce, then pour in 200 ml water and bring to a simmer.
Reduce to low, cover and cook 30–35 minutes until the beans are very soft and a knife slides easily into the potatoes.
Uncover and cook over medium heat for 3–5 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy and clings to the vegetables.
Stir through the parsley, adjust the salt, and serve warm or at room temperature.

batch_09_part_2.json::Indian Bhindi Masa.title: Bhindi masala
quick_steps: Dry the okra well, trim and slice into 2 cm pieces. Finely chop the onion and garlic, and chop the tomatoes.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the okra in batches for 8–10 minutes until browned and tender, then set aside.
Heat the remaining oil over medium heat and cook the onion for 6–7 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and chilli powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the tomatoes and salt and cook 8–10 minutes until a thick paste and the oil separates.
Return the okra and cook over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes until coated and heated through.
Stir through the garam masala and half the coriander leaves, then serve topped with the rest.

batch_09_part_2.json::German Rote Grutze.title: Rote Grütze (red berry pudding)
quick_steps: Set aside about 100 g of the berries to thaw in the fridge. Whisk the cornflour with 3 tbsp cold water until smooth, and finely grate 1 tsp lemon zest.
Heat the cherry juice, caster sugar and lemon zest in a medium saucepan over medium heat until the sugar dissolves, about 2 minutes.
Add the remaining berries and simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes, until soft and juicy.
Reduce to medium-low, re-whisk the cornflour mixture and pour it in. Cook for 1–2 minutes until glossy and coating a spoon, then take off the heat and fold in the reserved berries.
Spoon into four glasses and cool for 30 minutes. Cover and chill for at least 2 hours, until cold and softly set.
Serve cold, with the thickened cream poured over or alongside.

batch_09_part_2.json::French Tarte Flamb.title: Tarte flambée
quick_steps: Mix the flour, salt, water and olive oil into a dough, then knead for 3–4 minutes until smooth and elastic. Divide into 2 balls and cover.
Stir the nutmeg and pepper into the crème fraîche. Slice the onion very thinly and cut the bacon into 1 cm strips.
Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan) with 2 large trays inside. Rest the dough for 20 minutes.
Roll each ball on baking paper into a very thin oval, 2–3 mm thick. Spread with the crème fraîche mixture, leaving a 1 cm border, and top with the onion and bacon.
Slide onto the hot trays and bake for 10–12 minutes, until the edges are browned, the bacon is cooked and the onion is lightly charred.
Rest for 2 minutes, then cut and serve hot.

batch_09_part_2.json::French Ile Flottan.title: Île flottante
quick_steps: Separate the eggs, yolks in one bowl and whites in another. Heat the milk with the vanilla over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until steaming, then take off the heat.
Whisk the yolks with 50 g of the sugar until pale, then whisk in the warm milk. Cook in the pan over low heat for 6–8 minutes until it coats a spoon. Strain.
Cover the custard surface with baking paper and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until completely cold.
Beat the whites with the salt until foamy, then add 30 g of the sugar and beat until stiff and glossy. Simmer the water in a frying pan over medium-low heat.
Poach 4 large spoonfuls of meringue for 1 minute each side until puffed and firm. Drain. Melt the remaining 40 g sugar in a pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until amber.
Pour the cold custard into 4 bowls, float a meringue on each and drizzle with the caramel.

batch_09_part_2.json::Vietnamese Banh Xe.title: Bánh xèo
quick_steps: Whisk the rice flour, turmeric, salt, coconut milk, 250 ml water and spring onions into a smooth batter. Rest 20 minutes, thinning with a little water if thick.
Stir the lime juice from 2 limes, fish sauce, sugar, chilli and 60 ml water until the sugar dissolves. Cut the last lime into wedges.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the pork and garlic 3–4 minutes until cooked through, then the prawns 2–3 minutes until pink. Season with pepper and set aside.
Heat a little oil in the pan over medium-high. Pour in 125 ml batter, top with a quarter of the pork, prawns and bean sprouts, cover and cook 2 minutes.
Drizzle oil around the edge and cook over medium heat 3–4 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Fold, then repeat for 4 pancakes, keeping them warm in a 100°C oven.
Serve the pancakes torn up and wrapped in lettuce with the mint, coriander and lime wedges, dipped in the sauce.

batch_09_part_2.json::Italian Carciofi a.title: Carciofi alla romana
quick_steps: Squeeze one lemon into a large bowl of cold water. Snap the tough outer leaves off the artichokes until pale yellow-green, cut off the top third and peel the stems.
Rub all cut surfaces with the other lemon half, scoop out the fuzzy chokes and keep the artichokes in the lemon water.
Mix the garlic, parsley, mint, salt, pepper and 1 tbsp olive oil. Drain the artichokes and spoon the mixture into the centres and between the outer leaves.

Stand the artichokes stem-up in a snug saucepan with the water and remaining 2 tbsp olive oil. Simmer over medium heat, cover, then cook on low for 30–35 minutes, until a knife slips easily into the stems.
Uncover and simmer over medium heat for 3–5 minutes, until the juices turn glossy. Rest for 5 minutes, then serve warm with the juices and a squeeze of lemon.

batch_09_part_2.json::Finnish Lohikeitto.title: Lohikeitto
quick_steps: Cut the salmon into 3 cm cubes and chill. Cube the potatoes, dice the carrot, slice the leeks and rinse them well, and chop the dill.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the leeks and carrot with the salt for 6–7 minutes, until the leeks are soft and glossy but not browned.
Add the potatoes, chicken stock and 200 ml water. Boil over high heat, then simmer on medium-low for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides easily into a potato.
Reduce the heat to low. Add the salmon and cream and cook for 4–5 minutes, until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily. Don't let it boil.
Off the heat, stir in the dill, lemon juice and pepper. Season with more salt or lemon if needed and serve in warm bowls.

batch_09_part_2.json::Tunisian Lablabi.title: Lablabi
quick_steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Crush the garlic, juice the lemon, and tear the bread into bite-sized pieces into 4 deep bowls.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the garlic, ground cumin and cumin seeds for 30–60 seconds until fragrant, then stir in 1 tbsp harissa for 30 seconds.
Add the chickpeas, stock and salt, and bring to the boil over high heat. Reduce to medium-low and simmer for 20 minutes until the chickpeas are very tender.
Crush about a quarter of the chickpeas against the pan to thicken the broth. Stir in the lemon juice, simmer for 2 minutes, and season to taste.
Ladle the chickpeas and broth over the bread in the bowls. Top with the remaining harissa and serve straight away.

batch_09_part_2.json::British Bakewell T.title: Bakewell tart
quick_steps: Press the pastry into a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, prick the base and chill for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Line the pastry with baking paper and the rice. Bake for 15 minutes, remove the paper and rice, then bake 5 minutes more until pale golden and dry.
Beat the butter and caster sugar for 3–4 minutes until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs and vanilla, then fold in the almond meal and flour.
Spread the jam over the warm case, spoon the frangipane on top and smooth it to the edge. Scatter with the flaked almonds.
Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 30–35 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean. Foil the edge if it browns too fast.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then remove and dust with the icing sugar.

stages.title: Line the tin and chill
steps: Press the pastry sheet into a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, pushing it into the fluted edge and trimming the excess with a knife.
Prick the base all over with a fork.
Chill the lined tin in the fridge for 30 minutes so the pastry holds its shape.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) while the pastry chills.

stages.title: Blind-bake the case
steps: Line the chilled pastry with baking paper and fill with the uncooked rice.
Bake for 15 minutes, then lift out the paper and rice.
