Bake the empty case for a further 5 minutes until pale golden and dry, then cool in the tin for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Make the frangipane
steps: Beat the butter and caster sugar in a bowl with electric beaters for 3–4 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then add the vanilla extract; the mixture may look slightly curdled, which is fine.
Fold in the almond meal and plain flour until just combined.

stages.title: Assemble and bake
steps: Spread the raspberry jam evenly over the base of the warm pastry case.
Spoon the frangipane over the jam and smooth it to the edge, sealing it against the pastry.
Scatter the flaked almonds over the top.
Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 30–35 minutes until deep golden and set, and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cover the edge with foil if the pastry browns too quickly.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Cool the tart in the tin for 10 minutes so the jam settles and it slices cleanly.
Remove from the tin and dust with the icing sugar before slicing.

ingredients: 1 sheet shortcrust pastry (about 25 cm square), thawed
1 cup rice, uncooked, for weighing down the pastry (or baking beads)

batch_10.json::British Scotch Eggs.title: Scotch eggs
quick_steps: Boil four eggs for 6–7 minutes, cool in iced water, then peel carefully.
Mix the sausage mince with the mustard and seasoning. Flatten into four discs and wrap each around an egg, sealing the seams.
Coat each in flour, then the beaten eggs, then breadcrumbs.
Heat the frying oil to 170°C and fry for 7–9 minutes until golden and the sausage meat reaches 75°C.
Drain on a rack, rest for 3 minutes, then halve to serve.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Mix sausage mince with mustard and seasoning
flatten into four discs and wrap each around an egg, sealing seams.

stages.title: Cook the dish
steps: Coat in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs
heat the frying oil to 170°C and fry for 7–9 minutes until golden and sausage meat reaches 75°C.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Drain on a rack, rest 3 minutes and halve to serve.

batch_10.json::Turkish Kunefe.title: Künefe
quick_steps: Simmer the sugar, water and lemon juice in a saucepan over medium heat for 8 minutes, then cool the syrup completely.
Shred the kataifi, coat it evenly with the melted butter and press half into a 22 cm pan.
Spread the mozzarella over the pastry, leaving the edges clear, then cover with the remaining kataifi.
Cook over medium-low heat for 10 minutes each side, until golden.
Pour the cool syrup over the hot künefe, rest for 2 minutes and scatter with the pistachios.

batch_10.json::Italian Stracciatella Sou.title: Stracciatella soup
quick_steps: Bring the chicken stock to a gentle simmer in a large pot over medium heat.
Beat the eggs in a bowl with the grated Parmesan and nutmeg.
Add the baby spinach to the stock and wilt for 1 minute. Reduce the heat so the broth barely bubbles.
Pour in the egg mixture in a thin stream, stirring gently, and cook 1–2 minutes until set into soft ribbons.
Finish with grated lemon zest and black pepper, then serve immediately.

batch_09_part_2.json::Italian Ricotta Gn.title: Ricotta gnocchi
quick_steps: Drain the ricotta in a towel-lined sieve in the fridge for 25 minutes, until noticeably drier and crumbly.
Mix the ricotta with the egg, parmesan, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper until smooth. Gently fold in 100 g of the flour until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms.
Roll the dough into 2 cm ropes on a bench dusted with the remaining flour, cut into 2–3 cm pieces and chill on a floured tray for 10 minutes.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil over high heat with the remaining 3 tsp salt, then reduce to a simmer. Cook the dumplings in 2 batches for 2–3 minutes, until they float and are cooked through.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat until foaming. Add the sage and cook for 1–2 minutes, until nutty, golden-brown and crisp.
Toss the dumplings through the sage butter for 1 minute, until coated and lightly golden. Serve straight away.

batch_10.json::Spanish Salmorejo.title: Salmorejo
quick_steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, then cool and chop. Roughly cut the tomatoes and bread.
Blend the tomatoes, garlic and sherry vinegar until smooth. Add the bread and rest for 10 minutes to soften.
Blend again, streaming in the olive oil until thick and creamy. Chill for at least 1 hour.
Ladle into bowls and top with the chopped eggs, serrano ham and a drizzle of olive oil.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Boil eggs 9 minutes, cool and chop
roughly cut tomatoes and bread.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Blend tomatoes, garlic and vinegar until smooth
add bread and rest 10 minutes to soften.

stages.title: Cook the dish
steps: Blend again while streaming in olive oil until thick and creamy
chill at least 1 hour.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Ladle into bowls and garnish with chopped eggs, serrano ham and olive oil.

batch_10.json::Thai Pad See Ew.title: Pad see ew
quick_steps: Separate the noodles gently. Slice the chicken thinly and cut the Chinese broccoli stems and leaves separately.
Mix the light and dark soy sauces with the oyster sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok on high until smoking. Sear the chicken until cooked through, with no pink remaining.
Add the broccoli stems, then the leaves, and cook for 1 minute until the leaves are bright green and just wilted.
Push everything aside and scramble the eggs until just set. Add the noodles and sauce and toss on high for 2 minutes.
Let the noodles sit against the wok for 30 seconds until the edges char, then serve hot.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients

slice chicken thinly and cut broccoli stems and leaves separately.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Mix soy sauces and oyster sauce
heat oil in wok until smoking and sear chicken until cooked through.

stages.title: Cook the dish
steps: Add broccoli stems, then leaves, and cook for 1 minute until the leaves are bright green
push aside, scramble eggs, add noodles and sauce and toss on high heat for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Let noodles sit briefly against wok for charred edges, then serve hot.

batch_10.json::Greek Koulourakia.title: Greek koulourakia
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line trays. Cream the butter and sugar until light.
Beat in one egg, the orange juice and zest, then fold in the flour and baking powder to make a soft dough.
Roll small pieces of dough into ropes and twist into braids. Brush with the remaining beaten egg.
Bake for 18–22 minutes until pale gold.
Cool on the trays for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

batch_10.json::French Pain Perdu.title: Pain perdu
quick_steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar and vanilla in a shallow dish. Heat a large frying pan over medium heat.
Soak the brioche slices for 20–30 seconds per side, until the custard soaks in but the slices hold together.
Melt the butter in the pan, then cook the slices in batches for 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and the centre is set.
Serve straight away with the berries and a light dusting of icing sugar, if using.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Whisk eggs, milk, sugar and vanilla in a shallow dish
heat a skillet over medium.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Soak brioche 20–30 seconds per side so centre absorbs custard without falling apart.

stages.title: Cook the dish
steps: Melt butter in pan over medium heat and cook slices in batches 3–4 minutes per side until golden and centre is set.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Serve immediately with berries and a light dusting of icing sugar.

batch_10.json::Italian Torta Caprese.title: Torta caprese
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 170°C and line a 22 cm cake tin. Gently melt the chocolate and butter together until smooth.
Whisk the egg yolks with half the sugar until pale. Fold in the melted chocolate mixture, ground almonds and vanilla.
Whisk the egg whites with a pinch of salt and the remaining sugar to soft peaks. Gently fold into the chocolate mixture.
Pour into the tin and bake for 30–35 minutes, until the centre is just set.
Cool completely, then dust with icing sugar, if using, before slicing.

melt chocolate and butter gently.

stages.title: Build the flavours

fold in chocolate, almonds and vanilla.

stages.title: Cook the dish

stages.title: Finish and serve

batch_10.json::Korean Pajeon.title: Pajeon
quick_steps: Cut the spring onions into pan-length pieces. Whisk the plain flour, rice flour, cold water and egg into a thin batter.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Lay the spring onions across the pan and pour the batter over evenly.
Cook for 4–5 minutes until the underside is crisp. Flip carefully and cook 3–4 minutes more.
Mix the soy sauce and rice vinegar for dipping. Cut the pancake into wedges and serve hot.

stages.title: Cook the dish

stages.title: Finish and serve

cut pancake into wedges and serve hot.

batch_10.json::Spanish Tortilla de Espin.title: Tortilla de espinacas
quick_steps: Peel and thinly slice the potatoes, slice the onion and wash the spinach.
Cook the potatoes and onion in the olive oil in a pan over low heat for 15–20 minutes until tender, not browned. Wilt the spinach separately.
Beat the eggs with the salt, then fold in the drained potatoes, onion and spinach.
Pour into a non-stick pan over low heat and cook 6–8 minutes until set underneath. Flip carefully and cook 3 minutes more.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into wedges.

slice onion and wash spinach.

wilt spinach separately.

batch_10.json::Italian Insalata di Finoc.title: Insalata di finocchi
quick_steps: Trim the fennel bulbs and shave them very thinly.
Segment the oranges over a bowl to catch the juice.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and reserved orange juice with salt and pepper.
Gently toss the fennel, orange segments and black olives with the dressing until coated.
Scatter the parsley and fennel fronds over just before serving.

batch_10.json::Lebanese Riz bi Haleeb.title: Riz bi haleeb
quick_steps: Rinse the rice, then simmer it in a pot with 250 ml water over medium-low heat until the grains soften, about 12 minutes.
Add the milk and sugar and simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring so it doesn't stick.
Mix the cornflour with a little cold milk, stir it in and cook 3 minutes until thick.
Take off the heat and stir in the rosewater and orange blossom water.
Portion into bowls and chill. Scatter with chopped pistachios to serve.

batch_10.json::Chinese Hong Shao Rou.title: Hong shao rou
quick_steps: Cut the pork belly into 3 cm cubes, blanch in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Melt the rock sugar with 1 tbsp water in a pan over medium heat until amber.
Carefully add the pork and coat in the caramel. Add the ginger, spring onions, soy sauce, dark soy and Shaoxing wine.
Add water to barely cover, then the star anise. Cover and simmer on low for 75–90 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until glossy. Remove the aromatics and serve over steamed rice, if using.

batch_10.json::Moroccan Briouats.title: Moroccan briouats
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely dice the onion, then toast and chop the almonds until golden.
Cook the lamb and onion in a pan over medium-high heat until well browned and cooked through.
Stir in the cumin, cinnamon, almonds and parsley, then let the filling cool.
Cut the filo into strips and brush with melted butter. Add filling and fold into triangles.
Bake for 18–22 minutes until crisp and golden.
Rest for 3 minutes and serve with lemon wedges, if you like.

stir in cumin, cinnamon, almonds and parsley, then cool filling.

batch_09_part_2.json::Lebanese Shish Bar.title: Shish barak
quick_steps: Mix the flour, half the salt and 130 ml water into a dough. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth and elastic, then rest under a damp tea towel for 25 minutes.
Cook the onion in 1 tbsp of the oil in a pan over medium heat for 4 minutes. Add the lamb, cinnamon, remaining salt and pepper, and cook over medium-high until browned and no pink remains. Cool.
Roll the dough 2 mm thick and cut 6 cm circles. Fill each with 1 tsp of the filling, fold and seal, then pinch the corners together.
Toss the dumplings with the remaining oil and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 15–18 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.

Whisk the yoghurt, egg and cornflour in a saucepan, adding water if thick. Heat over medium until simmering, then simmer on low for 10 minutes until thickened. Add the dumplings and simmer for 5 minutes until tender.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat and fry the garlic for 1 minute until golden. Stir in the mint for 10 seconds, then spoon over the dumplings and serve.

batch_10.json::American Lemon Bars.title: Lemon bars
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 175°C and line a 20 cm square tin. Rub the butter into the plain flour and icing sugar until it comes together.
Press the mixture into the tin and bake for 18–20 minutes, until lightly golden.
Whisk the eggs, caster sugar, lemon juice and the 2 tbsp flour until smooth.
Pour the filling over the hot base and bake for 20–25 minutes, until set.
Cool completely, then chill for 2 hours before dusting with icing sugar and slicing.

batch_10.json::Italian Minestra Maritata.title: Minestra maritata
quick_steps: Mix the pork mince with the egg, breadcrumbs and half the Parmesan. Roll into 2 cm meatballs.
Bring the chicken stock to a simmer in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced carrot and celery and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the meatballs and simmer for 8–10 minutes, until cooked through with no pink in the middle.
Add the small pasta and cook to packet time, adding the kale for the final 3 minutes, until tender.
Ladle into bowls and top with the remaining Parmesan and pepper.

stages.title: Cook the dish
steps: Add meatballs and simmer 8–10 minutes until cooked through
add pasta and cook according to packet, then kale for final 3 minutes.

batch_10_part_2.json::Japanese Zaru Soba.title: Zaru soba
quick_steps: Simmer the dashi, soy sauce and mirin in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes, then chill for at least 30 minutes until completely cold.
Thinly slice the spring onions and cut the nori into thin strips. Fill a large bowl with cold water and ice.
Boil the soba in a large pot over high heat for 4–6 minutes, until tender with a slight bite.
Drain, then rinse under cold water, rubbing gently, until the water runs clear and the noodles are cold. Plunge into the iced water for 30 seconds and drain well.
Divide the noodles among 4 plates or trays and top with the nori. Serve the chilled sauce in small bowls, with the spring onions and wasabi to stir in before dipping.

batch_10.json::Mexican Sopes.title: Sopes
quick_steps: Mix the masa harina, warm water and salt into a soft dough. Rest it covered for 10 minutes, then shape eight thick discs.
Cook the discs in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes each side. While still warm, pinch the edges into raised rims.
Return the sopes to the pan over medium heat with the oil. Cook 2 minutes each side until crisp.
Warm the refried beans separately until hot.
Fill each sope with beans, salsa, crumbled queso fresco and sliced avocado.

rest covered 10 minutes, then shape eight thick discs.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Cook discs in a dry skillet over medium heat 2 minutes each side
while warm, pinch edges into raised rims.

stages.title: Cook the dish
steps: Return to pan with a little oil and cook 2 minutes each side until crisp
warm refried beans separately.

stages.title: Finish and serve

batch_10_part_2.json::Greek Revithada.title: Revithada
quick_steps: Soak the chickpeas in plenty of cold water for 8 hours or overnight, then drain and rinse well.
Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Put the chickpeas, onions, bay leaves, half the olive oil and 1 litre water in a heavy lidded casserole.
Bring to the boil on the stovetop over medium-high heat, then simmer gently about 5 minutes, skimming the foam until little new foam forms.
Cover and bake for 3 hours, until the chickpeas crush easily. Top up with boiling water if they poke out.
Discard the bay leaves, then stir in the salt, pepper, lemon juice and remaining olive oil. Mash a handful of chickpeas until the broth turns thick and creamy.
Rest, covered, for 15 minutes, then taste and add more salt if needed.

batch_10_part_2.json::Indian Aloo Parath.title: Aloo paratha
quick_steps: Mix the atta flour, half the salt and 180 ml water into a soft dough. Knead for 3–4 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water over high heat, then simmer on medium for 12–15 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain and steam-dry for 5 minutes.
Mash the potatoes smooth, then mix in the chilli, cumin seeds, garam masala, coriander and remaining salt. Cool for 5 minutes and roll into 6 balls.
Divide the dough into 6 balls. Flatten each, enclose a potato ball, seal well, then roll into an 18 cm round using the extra flour for dusting.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes. Cook each paratha for 1 minute until pale spots appear, then flip and brush with melted butter.
Cook 30–60 seconds each side, brushing the other side with butter, until golden brown with darker spots. Keep wrapped in a tea towel and serve hot.

batch_10_part_2.json::Korean Kongnamul G.title: Kongnamul guk
quick_steps: Rinse the soybean sprouts, discarding any slimy or discoloured ones and loose husks. Finely chop the garlic and thinly slice the spring onions.
Bring the vegetable stock to the boil in a medium saucepan over high heat, about 5 minutes.
Add the sprouts and garlic, cover and reduce to medium heat. Simmer for 7 minutes without lifting the lid, until tender with a little crunch.
Stir in the soy sauce and salt, then simmer uncovered for 2 minutes. Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
Stir in the spring onions and sesame oil, then turn off the heat. Ladle into bowls and serve hot.

batch_10_part_2.json::Peruvian Arroz Cha.title: Arroz chaufa
quick_steps: Break up the cold rice. Toss the chicken with the salt and pepper. Mix the soy sauce and sesame oil together, and keep the spring onion whites and greens separate.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering. Scramble the eggs for 30–40 seconds until just set, then break up and set aside.
Heat the remaining vegetable oil in the wok over high heat. Cook the chicken for 5–6 minutes until golden and cooked through with no pink in the centre.
Add the garlic and spring onion whites and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the rice and toss over high heat for 3–4 minutes until steaming hot. Pour in the soy and sesame oil mixture and toss for 1 minute until evenly coloured.
Return the eggs, toss for 30 seconds, then stir through the spring onion greens and serve straight away.

batch_10_part_2.json::Filipino Arroz Cal.title: Arroz caldo
quick_steps: Rinse the rice and drain. Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat, then cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the chicken and cook for 4–5 minutes until opaque on the outside.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the stock and 500 ml water. Bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce to low and simmer, partly covered, for 40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the rice has broken down and thickened and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the fish sauce and pepper, loosening with a little hot water if too thick. Serve topped with the spring onions and the lime wedges.

batch_10_part_2.json::Syrian Fatteh.title: Fatteh
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Toss the torn pita with the olive oil on a tray and bake 8–10 minutes until golden and crisp.
Mix the yoghurt, garlic, 2 tbsp lemon juice and half the salt until smooth. Add more lemon juice if you want it sharper.
Simmer the chickpeas in a saucepan over medium heat with 125 ml water, the cumin and remaining salt for 5–6 minutes, until hot and mostly reduced.
Melt the butter in a small frying pan over medium-low heat. Cook the pine nuts 2–3 minutes until golden brown, then remove from the heat.
Layer the pita, warm chickpeas and a little of their liquid in 4 bowls. Top with the yoghurt and pine nut butter, scatter with the parsley and serve.

batch_10_part_2.json::Ethiopian Atakilt.title: Atakilt wat
quick_steps: Cut the cabbage into wide strips, and cube the potatoes and carrots. Finely dice the onion and chop the garlic; grate the ginger.
Heat the oil in a large, deep pan over medium heat. Cook the onion with the salt for 8 minutes until soft and translucent, not browned.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and turmeric for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the potatoes and carrots to coat.
Add 150 ml water, simmer gently, cover and cook for 12 minutes until the vegetables just soften at the edges.
Stir in the cabbage and black pepper, cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes until the potato is tender and the cabbage is soft.
Uncover and cook over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until the excess liquid evaporates. Season to taste and serve warm.

batch_10_part_2.json::Georgian Badrijani.title: Badrijani nigvzit
quick_steps: Slice the eggplants lengthways into 5 mm strips, sprinkle both sides with the salt and leave for 20 minutes. Rinse briefly and pat very dry.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the strips in batches, 2–3 minutes each side until soft and golden, adding the remaining oil as needed.
Blitz the walnuts, garlic and coriander to a fine paste. Add the vinegar and 2–3 tbsp water until smooth but thick, then stir in half the parsley.
Drain the strips and let them cool in a single layer for 10 minutes, until cool to the touch.
Spread each strip with about 1 tbsp of paste, roll up from the narrow end and place seam side down. Scatter with the remaining parsley and the pomegranate seeds, if using.

batch_10_part_2.json::Japanese Ochazuke.title: Ochazuke
quick_steps: Season the salmon with the salt. Cook in the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat, skin-side down for 4–5 minutes until crisp, then turn and cook 2–3 minutes until the flesh flakes easily.
Remove the skin and bones from the salmon, then flake the flesh into large pieces.
Slice the spring onions and nori thinly. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until lightly golden.
Microwave the rice, covered, for 2–3 minutes until steaming hot, then divide among four bowls.
Heat the green tea with the soy sauce in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until steaming but not boiling.
Top the rice with the salmon, spring onions, nori and sesame seeds, then pour over the hot tea and serve.

batch_10_part_2.json::Persian Mast o Khi.title: Mast o khiar
quick_steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for about 3 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Cool, then roughly chop.
Finely dice the cucumbers and toss with the salt in a sieve. Drain for 5 minutes, then press and pat dry. Roughly chop the sultanas.
Stir the yoghurt until smooth, then mix in the dried mint (rubbed between your palms) and the garlic.
Fold through the cucumber, sultanas and two-thirds of the walnuts.
Cover and chill for 25 minutes. Add a pinch more salt if needed.
Top with the remaining walnuts and the rose petals just before serving.

batch_10_part_2.json::Italian Polenta co.title: Polenta con funghi
quick_steps: Slice the mushrooms, chop the garlic, pick the thyme leaves and finely grate the parmesan.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms in batches for 6–8 minutes, until deep golden and dry.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Season with half the salt and the pepper, then cover to keep warm off the heat.
Bring the stock and remaining salt to the boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce to medium-low and whisk in the polenta in a thin stream.
Cook for 3–5 minutes until thick and pulling away from the pan. Off the heat, stir in the remaining butter and the parmesan until smooth.
Spoon the polenta into warmed bowls and top with the mushrooms, pan juices and extra pepper.

batch_10_part_2.json::Indian Upma.title: Upma
quick_steps: Dice the onion and carrot finely, juice the lemon, and measure out the peas, semolina and water.
Toast the semolina in a large, deep frying pan over low-medium heat for 4–5 minutes until nutty and slightly darker. Tip into a bowl.
Heat the oil in the same pan over medium heat. Cook the mustard seeds until they pop, then add the curry leaves for 10 seconds.
Add the onion, carrot and salt and cook for 4–5 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent.
Add the water and peas and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce to low, pour in the semolina in a slow stream, then cover and cook 2–3 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Stir in the lemon juice, fluff with a fork and serve hot.

batch_10_part_2.json::Mexican Calabacita.title: Calabacitas
quick_steps: Dice the zucchini, tomatoes, onion and chilli. Rinse frozen corn in a sieve under warm water to thaw, then drain well.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes until soft, then add the chilli for 1 minute until fragrant.
Turn the heat to medium-high and cook the zucchini with the salt for 5–6 minutes until golden at the edges and just tender.
Add the corn and tomatoes and cook for 3–4 minutes until the tomatoes soften and release their juices but the zucchini holds its shape.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed. Scatter the feta and coriander over and serve straight away.

batch_10_part_2.json::Japanese Yaki Onig.title: Yaki onigiri
quick_steps: Spread the warm rice on a tray for 5 minutes until easy to handle but still sticky. Mix through the salt and sesame seeds.
With wet hands, divide the rice into 8 portions of about 75 g. Press each into a firm triangle about 2 cm thick, with no cracks.
Stir the soy sauce, mirin and sesame oil together in a small bowl for the glaze. Keep it and a pastry brush by the stove.
Heat half the vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook 4 onigiri for 4–5 minutes each side, until golden, crisp and releasing easily.
Brush both sides with glaze, cooking 30 seconds per side until it sizzles and darkens. Repeat with the remaining oil and onigiri.

batch_10_part_2.json::Italian Semolina G.title: Semolina gnocchi alla romana
quick_steps: Grease a 20 x 30 cm tray with a little of the 40 g butter and line it with baking paper. Split the parmesan into two 45 g portions and lightly whisk the egg yolks.
Heat the milk and salt in a large saucepan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until steaming. Reduce to low and whisk in the semolina in a slow stream.
Stir for 8–10 minutes until very thick and pulling away from the pan sides. Off the heat, beat in 30 g butter, the egg yolks and half the parmesan until glossy.
Spread onto the tray 1.5 cm thick, cool for 15 minutes, then chill for 30 minutes until completely firm.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut into 5 cm rounds and overlap them in a greased baking dish, pressing trimmings into any gaps.
Dot with the remaining butter, scatter over the remaining parmesan and bake 20–25 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

batch_10_part_2.json::Brazilian Farofa.title: Farofa
quick_steps: Cook the bacon in a large frying pan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, until golden and crisp. Lift it out onto a plate, leaving the fat in the pan.
Add the butter to the bacon fat over medium heat. When it foams, add the onion and cook for 5–6 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Reduce to medium-low, add the cassava flour and stir constantly for 4–5 minutes, until golden and sandy with no raw floury smell.
Stir in the bacon, parsley, salt and a few grinds of pepper. Taste, adjust the salt and serve warm.

batch_10_part_2.json::Vietnamese Ca Kho.title: Cá kho tộ (caramelised fish)
quick_steps: Cut the fish into 4 cm pieces and pat dry. Chop the garlic and shallots, and slice the spring onions and chilli for serving.
Heat the oil in a small heavy-based saucepan or clay pot over medium heat, add the sugar and cook for 4–5 minutes until deep amber.
Stir in the garlic and shallots for 1 minute until fragrant. Carefully add the water (it spits), stir until the caramel dissolves, then add the fish sauce.
Simmer over medium-low heat. Add the fish in a single layer and cook 6 minutes, then turn and cook 5–6 minutes more until cooked through and flaking. Cook the rice to packet directions meanwhile.
Lift out the fish and keep warm. Boil the sauce over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes until syrupy, then return the fish for 1 minute to coat.
Top with the pepper, spring onions and chilli, and serve with the rice.

batch_10_part_2.json::Korean Gyeran Jjim.title: Gyeran jjim
quick_steps: Cool the stock if warm. Gently whisk the eggs, then mix in the stock, fish sauce and salt.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a heatproof 1 litre bowl and skim off any bubbles. Cover loosely with foil.
Set a rack in a wide pot with water 3 cm below it. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce to medium-low.
Lower in the bowl, cover the pot and steam for 12–15 minutes, until the surface is set with only a slight centre wobble.
Rest the custard for 2 minutes. Top with the sliced spring onions and sesame oil, and serve hot.

batch_10_part_2.json::Italian Bresaola R.title: Bresaola rucola e grana
quick_steps: Wash and thoroughly dry the rocket. Shave the parmesan into thin curls with a vegetable peeler and chill them, along with four plates.
Zest the lemon, then juice it. Whisk 2 tbsp of the juice with the olive oil, black pepper and salt, and add more juice if you want it sharper.
Lay the bresaola in a single slightly overlapping layer on the chilled plates, 40 g per plate. Rest for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Toss the rocket with half the dressing until lightly coated, then pile it over the bresaola.
Top with the parmesan curls and lemon zest, drizzle with the remaining dressing and serve straight away.

batch_10_part_2.json::Greek Melitzanosal.title: Melitzanosalata
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Prick the eggplants all over and roast on a lined tray for 40–45 minutes, turning once, until charred and completely soft.
Cool the eggplants for 10 minutes, then scoop the flesh into a fine sieve, discarding the skins. Drain for 15 minutes, pressing gently once or twice.
Roughly chop the flesh and combine in a bowl with the garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Stir in the olive oil a little at a time until creamy but still chunky, then fold through the parsley.
Rest covered at room temperature for 15 minutes, then taste and adjust the salt or lemon juice.
Warm the pita in the oven for 2–3 minutes if you like, and serve with the dip.

batch_10_part_2.json::Japanese Sunomono.title: Sunomono
quick_steps: Thinly slice the cucumbers, toss with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, until softened and watery.
Soak the wakame in 500 ml cold water for 5 minutes, until soft and fully expanded. Drain, squeeze dry and cut long pieces into bite-sized lengths.
Whisk the rice vinegar, sugar and soy sauce for about 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until lightly golden.
Rinse the cucumber, squeeze out as much liquid as you can, then toss gently with the wakame and dressing. Chill for 10 minutes.
Serve cold in small bowls, topped with the toasted sesame seeds.

batch_10_part_2.json::Egyptian Basbousa.title: Basbousa
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease a 20 cm square tin with extra butter and line the base. Mix the semolina, caster sugar and baking powder.
Stir in the yoghurt and melted butter until just combined, then rest the batter for 5 minutes.
Spoon the batter into the tin and smooth the top. Cut into 12 pieces almost to the base and press an almond into each.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until deep golden and a skewer in the centre comes out clean.
Meanwhile, simmer the white sugar, water and lemon peel in a saucepan over medium heat for about 8 minutes, until slightly syrupy. Stir in the lemon juice and discard the peel.
Pour the warm syrup over the hot cake and re-cut the score lines. Leave in the tin for at least 1 hour, until cooled and the syrup is absorbed.

batch_10_part_2.json::Spanish Espinacas.title: Espinacas con garbanzos
quick_steps: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium heat. Fry the torn bread for 2–3 minutes until golden, then add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant and pale golden.
Tip the bread and garlic into a small blender, leaving the oil in the pan. Blend with the paprika, cumin, red wine vinegar and 100 ml stock for 1 minute until a thick, mostly smooth paste forms.
Return the pan to medium heat with the remaining 1 tbsp oil and the chickpeas. Add the remaining 150 ml stock and simmer for 8 minutes until reduced by about half.
Stir in the paste and the salt, and cook for 3 minutes until the sauce is thick and clings to the chickpeas.
Add the spinach a handful at a time, stirring until wilted, about 3–4 minutes. Simmer 2 minutes more until no watery liquid pools.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed, then serve hot with the lemon wedges.

batch_10_part_2.json::Turkish Mercimek K.title: Mercimek köfte (lentil köfte)
quick_steps: Rinse the red lentils, then boil them in 600 ml water with the salt over high heat. Reduce to medium-low and simmer 12–15 minutes until collapsed, thick and mushy.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the bulgur, cover and leave 15 minutes until swollen and a firm paste.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion 6–7 minutes until soft and golden, then add the tomato paste and cumin and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Mix the onion mixture into the lentils, then add the spring onions, parsley and lemon juice. Mix with damp hands until it holds together when squeezed, then cool 5 minutes.
Shape heaped tablespoons into small ovals about 6 cm long, making about 20. Serve warm or at room temperature in the lettuce leaves.

batch_10_part_2.json::Indian Dhokla.title: Dhokla
quick_steps: Sift the chickpea flour into a bowl, then whisk in the yoghurt, 120 ml water, turmeric, salt and half the sugar for 2 minutes until smooth. Rest 10 minutes. Oil a 20 cm cake tin.
Bring 3 cm water to the boil in a wide pot with a rack over high heat, then reduce to medium to keep it steadily simmering.
Whisk the fruit salt into the batter until frothy and paler. Pour into the tin, set on the rack, cover and steam 15–18 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool the dhokla in the tin for 10 minutes, then run a knife around the edge and turn it out onto a board.
Heat the remaining oil in a small pan over medium heat, then cook the mustard seeds until they pop. Add the curry leaves and chilli for 15 seconds.
Add 2 tbsp water and the remaining sugar, simmer 1 minute until dissolved. Spoon over the dhokla squares and scatter with the coriander.

batch_10_part_2.json::Korean Sigeumchi N.title: Sigeumchi namul
quick_steps: Wash the spinach in cold water until no grit remains, then bring 2 litres of water and the salt to a rolling boil over high heat. Prepare a bowl of iced water.
Blanch the spinach for 30–45 seconds, until the stems are just tender and the leaves bright green. Move it straight into the iced water for 1 minute until cold.
Squeeze the spinach firmly until no more water drips out, then cut it into 5 cm lengths and shake loose into a bowl.
Add the garlic, sesame oil and soy sauce, then toss by hand for about 30 seconds until every strand is coated. Add a pinch more salt only if needed.
Pile into a serving bowl and scatter over the sesame seeds and spring onion.

batch_10_part_2.json::Chinese Liangban H.title: Liangban huanggua
quick_steps: Trim the cucumbers and smash them with a rolling pin until they crack along their length. Tear or cut into 3 cm chunks.
Toss the cucumber with the salt and stand for 10 minutes. Drain well and pat dry with paper towel.
Whisk the garlic, black vinegar, soy sauce, chilli oil, sesame oil and sugar for about 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the cucumbers through the dressing until every piece is coated. Serve straight away, or chill for up to 15 minutes.

batch_10_part_2.json::Austrian Topfenstr.title: Topfenstrudel
quick_steps: Drain the ricotta in a paper towel-lined sieve for 10 minutes. Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and zest the lemon.
Mix the drained ricotta with the egg, caster sugar and lemon zest until smooth and thick, then fold in the sultanas.
Spoon the filling in a log down the centre of the puff pastry on a lined tray, leaving a 3 cm border at each end. Fold the sides over, seal the ends and turn seam-side down.
Brush with half the melted butter. Bake for 30–35 minutes, until deep golden and puffed and the filling feels set.
Brush with the remaining butter and rest for 15 minutes. Dust with icing sugar, slice and serve warm.

batch_10_part_2.json::French Tarte Fine.title: Tarte fine aux pommes
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Lay the puff pastry on a lined tray, score a border 1.5 cm in and prick the centre with a fork.
Juice the lemon into a bowl. Thinly slice the apples (2–3 mm, skin on) and toss them in the juice.
Arrange the apples in overlapping rows inside the border. Brush with the melted butter and sprinkle with the caster sugar.
Bake on the middle shelf for 30 minutes, until the border is deep golden and the apple edges are browned. Cover loosely with foil if the apples brown too fast.
Meanwhile, warm the apricot jam with 1 tsp water in a small saucepan over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until runny. Brush it over the hot tart.
Rest the tart on the tray for 10 minutes, until the pastry firms up, then cut into 4 pieces.

batch_11_part_1.json::Lebanese Manakish.title: Manakish za'atar
quick_steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, warm water and 2 tbsp olive oil into a soft dough. Knead for 8 minutes, then cover and rest 60 minutes until puffy.
Heat the oven to 230°C with a tray inside.
Divide the dough into four balls and roll into thin rounds. Mix the za'atar with the extra virgin olive oil.
Spread the za'atar oil over each round, leaving a narrow border.
Bake on the hot tray for 8–10 minutes until blistered. Cool briefly before serving.

batch_11_part_1.json::Greek Pastitsio.title: Pastitsio
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Cook the pasta in boiling water on high for 2 minutes less than the packet says, then drain. Lightly whisk the eggs and grate the Parmesan.
Brown the onion and beef in the olive oil over medium-high heat for about 10 minutes until the beef is browned. Add the crushed tomatoes and cinnamon and simmer for 15 minutes.
Melt the butter over medium heat, stir in the flour, then gradually whisk in the milk. Cook until thick.
Cool the béchamel slightly, then whisk in the eggs and half the Parmesan.
Layer the pasta, meat sauce and béchamel in a dish, top with the remaining Parmesan and bake for 35–40 minutes until golden. Rest for 15 minutes before slicing.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Heat oven to 190°C.
Cook pasta in boiling water on high heat 2 minutes short of packet directions; drain.
Whisk eggs lightly and grate cheese.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Brown onion and beef in oil for 10 minutes; add tomatoes and cinnamon and simmer 15 minutes.
Melt butter, stir in flour and gradually whisk in milk; cook until thick.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Cool béchamel slightly, whisk in eggs and half the cheese.
Layer pasta, meat sauce and béchamel in a dish; top with cheese and bake 35–40 minutes.
Rest 15 minutes before slicing.

batch_10_part_2.json::Persian Adas Polo.title: Adas polo
quick_steps: Rinse the basmati rice, then soak it in 1 litre cold water with 1 tbsp salt for 20 minutes. Thinly slice the onions meanwhile.
Boil the brown lentils in 750 ml water over high heat, then simmer on medium-low for 15–20 minutes until tender but holding their shape. Drain and season with 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper.

Cook the onions in the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium heat for 15–18 minutes until deep golden. Add the sultanas and cinnamon for 2 minutes until plump, then stir half through the lentils.
Parboil the drained rice in salted boiling water in a large non-stick pot over high heat for 5–6 minutes, until soft outside but firm in the centre. Drain and rinse briefly.
Melt half the butter in the wiped pot over medium heat. Layer in the rice and lentils into a pyramid, poke steam holes through it and dot with the remaining butter.

Cover with a tea towel-wrapped lid and cook on medium-high for 5 minutes, then on the lowest heat for 25 minutes until the rice is fluffy and the base has a golden crust. Top with the reserved onions.

batch_11_part_1.json::French Cassoulet-I.title: Cassoulet-inspired white beans
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Drain the beans, dice the onion and carrots, and slice the sausages into large pieces.
Brown the sausages in 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat for 6 minutes until browned all over. Set aside.
Soften the onion and carrots in the remaining oil over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, tomatoes, thyme, beans and stock.
Return the sausages to the pan and simmer for 10 minutes until the sausages are cooked through, then transfer to a baking dish.
Scatter over the breadcrumbs and bake uncovered for 25 minutes, until bubbling and golden.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Heat oven to 190°C.
Drain beans, dice vegetables and slice sausages into large pieces.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Brown sausages in 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat for 6 minutes and set aside.
Soften onion and carrots in remaining oil over medium heat for 8 minutes; add garlic, tomatoes, thyme, beans and stock.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Return sausages to the pan, simmer 10 minutes, then transfer to a baking dish.
Scatter breadcrumbs and bake uncovered 25 minutes until bubbling and golden.

batch_11_part_1.json::French Lentil Sala.title: French lentil salad with mustard
quick_steps: Rinse the lentils and simmer with the bay leaf in plenty of water over medium heat for 20–25 minutes, until tender but still holding their shape. Drain well.
Mince the shallot and dice the celery.
Whisk the Dijon mustard, red wine vinegar and olive oil with salt and pepper.
Toss the warm lentils with the dressing, then fold through the shallot, celery and parsley.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

batch_11_part_1.json::Chinese Congee wit.title: Congee with ginger chicken
quick_steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Slice the ginger and spring onions, and cut the chicken into two even pieces.
Combine the rice, stock and ginger in a saucepan. Simmer uncovered on low heat for 45–55 minutes, until the grains break down.
Add the chicken for the final 15–20 minutes, until cooked through.
Remove the chicken and shred it with forks.
Return the chicken to the congee and thin with hot water. Season with the soy sauce and salt.
Finish with the spring onion and sesame oil.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Rinse rice until water runs mostly clear.
Slice ginger and spring onions; cut chicken into two even pieces.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Combine rice, stock and ginger in a saucepan; simmer uncovered on low heat 45–55 minutes, stirring often, until grains break down.
Add chicken for the final 15–20 minutes, still on low heat, and cook through.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Remove chicken and shred with forks.
Return to porridge, adjust thickness with hot water and season with soy and salt; finish with spring onion and sesame oil.

batch_11_part_1.json::Portuguese Bacalha.title: Bacalhau à Brás
quick_steps: Pat the desalted cod dry and flake it, removing all bones. Cut the potatoes into thin matchsticks.
Fry the potatoes in batches over medium heat until golden, then drain.
Soften the onion in the olive oil for 10 minutes, then add the garlic and cod. Cook 5 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes.
Beat the eggs lightly. Fold the potatoes into the cod, reduce the heat and stir in the eggs until softly set.
Finish with the parsley and olives, then serve.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Use cod that has been thoroughly desalted according to supplier instructions.
Pat dry and flake, removing all bones; cut potatoes into thin matchsticks.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Fry potatoes in batches over medium heat until golden and drain.
Soften onion in olive oil for 10 minutes, add garlic and cod, and cook 5 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Beat eggs lightly.
Fold potatoes into cod mixture, reduce heat and stir in eggs until softly set; finish with parsley and olives.

batch_11_part_1.json::Mexican Elote Sala.title: Elote salad
quick_steps: Remove the husks and silk from the corn. Zest and juice the lime, crumble the feta or cotija and chop the coriander.
Char the corn in a dry skillet over high heat, or on a grill, for 10–12 minutes, turning until browned in patches.
Cool the corn slightly, then cut the kernels from the cobs.
Mix the mayonnaise, sour cream, lime zest and juice, and chilli powder.
Toss the warm corn through the dressing, scatter the cheese and coriander over the top and serve.

batch_11_part_2.json::Indian Paneer Bhur.title: Paneer bhurji
quick_steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until lightly golden, about 5 minutes.
Add the ginger and green chilli and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, cumin and salt. Cook until the tomatoes collapse and most of the liquid evaporates.
Stir in the garam masala, then add the crumbled paneer and gently fold through for 2–3 minutes until heated through.
Finish with the coriander and serve with toast or roti.

batch_11_part_2.json::Indian Vegetable P.title: Vegetable pulao
quick_steps: Rinse the basmati until the water runs mostly clear, then soak for 10 minutes and drain well.
Heat the ghee in a lidded saucepan over medium heat. Fry the cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and bay leaf for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook until lightly golden. Stir in the carrot and drained rice for 1 minute.
Add the water, peas and salt and bring to a simmer. Cover tightly and cook on low for 12 minutes.
Turn off the heat and rest covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir through the lemon juice.

stages.title: Rinse and soak rice
steps: Rinse basmati under cool water until it runs mostly clear to remove surface starch.
Soak 10 minutes while preparing vegetables, then drain thoroughly.

stages.title: Toast aromatics
steps: Heat ghee in a lidded saucepan over medium heat; fry cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and bay leaf for 30 seconds.
Add onion and cook until lightly golden, then stir in carrot and drained rice for 1 minute.

stages.title: Steam the rice
steps: Add water, peas and salt; bring to a simmer, cover tightly and cook on low for 12 minutes.
Turn off heat and rest covered for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork and add lemon juice.

batch_11_part_2.json::Korean Dakdoritang.title: Dakdoritang
quick_steps: Pat the chicken dry and trim excess fat. Mix the soy sauce, gochugaru, gochujang, sugar and garlic with 3 tbsp water.
Put the chicken, onion and 500 ml water in a wide pot over medium heat. Bring to a simmer and skim off any foam.
Stir in the sauce and simmer partly covered for 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrot. Simmer 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the chicken reaches 74°C at its thickest point.
Uncover for the last few minutes to thicken the broth. Scatter the spring onions over the top.

batch_11_part_1.json::Vietnamese Lemongr.title: Lemongrass tofu rice bowls
quick_steps: Press the tofu for 15 minutes, then cube it. Cook the jasmine rice to packet directions, slice the cucumber and julienne the carrot.
Mix the lemongrass, garlic, soy sauce and sugar in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu for 8–10 minutes until golden.
Add the lemongrass mixture and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Mix the lime juice, rice vinegar and 1 tbsp water for the dressing.
Divide the rice among bowls, top with the tofu, cucumber and carrot, then drizzle with the dressing.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Press tofu for 15 minutes and cut into cubes.
Rinse rice and cook according to packet; slice cucumber and julienne carrot.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Mix lemongrass, garlic, soy and sugar.
Pan-fry tofu in oil over medium-high heat 8–10 minutes until golden, then add lemongrass mixture and cook 2 minutes until fragrant.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Mix lime juice and vinegar with 1 tbsp water.
Divide rice among bowls, add tofu and fresh vegetables, and drizzle with dressing.

batch_11_part_2.json::Peruvian Papa a la.title: Papa a la huancaína
quick_steps: Boil the whole potatoes in salted water until a knife slips in easily, about 18–20 minutes. Drain, cool slightly, then peel if you like and cut into thick slices.
Blend the feta, evaporated milk, aji amarillo paste, crackers and oil until smooth, adding a little water if it's too thick. Taste before salting.
Arrange the lettuce leaves and potato slices on a platter.
Spoon the sauce generously over the potatoes and garnish with quartered hard-boiled eggs and black olives.

batch_11_part_2.json::Sri Lankan Pol Sam.title: Pol sambol
quick_steps: Finely mince the red onion and chilli, removing the chilli seeds if you prefer less heat. Combine with the salt and chilli flakes in a mortar or sturdy bowl.
Lightly pound the onion mixture until it turns juicy and well combined, about 2 minutes.
Add the coconut and lime juice and mix until evenly seasoned and the coconut is lightly coloured.
Taste and adjust the salt, heat and lime, then serve straight away with rice, if using.

batch_11_part_2.json::Indonesian Sayur L.title: Sayur lodeh
quick_steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger and turmeric with a splash of water to a coarse paste. Bruise the lemongrass with the back of a knife.
Fry the paste in the oil over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until fragrant and slightly darkened. Add the lemongrass and cook for another minute.
Pour in the water and coconut milk, then add the carrot and aubergine. Simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Add the green beans and cabbage and cook until just tender, keeping the broth below a hard boil.

stages.title: Prepare paste
steps: Blend shallots, garlic, ginger and turmeric with a splash of water to a coarse paste.
Bruise lemongrass with the back of a knife to release aroma.

stages.title: Cook aromatics
steps: Fry spice paste in oil over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Add lemongrass and stir for another minute.

stages.title: Simmer vegetables
steps: Pour in water and coconut milk, then add carrot and aubergine; simmer gently 10 minutes.
Add beans and cabbage and cook until just tender, keeping the broth below a hard boil.

batch_11_part_2.json::Georgian Chakhokhb.title: Chakhokhbili
quick_steps: Pat the chicken dry, season, and brown in the oil over medium-high heat, about 3 minutes each side. Set aside on a plate.
Soften the onions and sliced red pepper in the same pan for about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ground coriander until fragrant.
Return the chicken with its juices, add the tomatoes, then cover and simmer gently for 18–20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74°C.
Scatter over the coriander leaves and serve with bread, if using.

batch_11_part_2.json::Italian Bagna Caud.title: Bagna cauda
quick_steps: Cut the carrots, celery, capsicum and fennel into long dipping sticks. Arrange on a platter and keep chilled until serving.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a small saucepan over very low heat.
Add the sliced garlic and cook gently for 10–12 minutes, until completely soft but not browned.
Add the anchovies and stir until they dissolve into the warm oil.
Serve the dip warm in a heatproof bowl with the raw vegetables.

batch_11_part_2.json::Greek Spanakorizo.title: Spanakorizo
quick_steps: Heat the olive oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Soften the onion for 5–6 minutes, then add the spring onions and cook 1 minute until softened.
Stir in the rice, then add the spinach in handfuls until wilted.
Add the stock and a pinch of salt. Cover and simmer gently for 18–20 minutes until the rice is tender, adding a little hot water if needed.
Remove from the heat and rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fold in the chopped dill, lemon juice and zest. Drizzle with a little more olive oil and season with salt and pepper.

stages.title: Soften aromatics
steps: Heat olive oil in a deep pan over medium heat and soften onion for 5–6 minutes.
Add spring onions and cook for 1 minute until softened, before stirring in rice.

stages.title: Wilt spinach and simmer
steps: Add spinach in handfuls, stirring until wilted; add stock and a pinch of salt.
Cover and simmer gently for 18–20 minutes until rice is tender, adding a little hot water if needed.

stages.title: Finish with lemon
steps: Remove from heat and rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fold in chopped dill, lemon juice and zest; drizzle with olive oil and season to taste.

batch_11_part_2.json::Mexican Rajas con.title: Rajas con crema
quick_steps: Char the poblano peppers under a hot grill, turning until the skins blister all over.
Cover for 10 minutes, then peel, deseed and slice into strips.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Soften the onion until translucent and lightly golden.
Add the pepper strips and corn, and cook until warmed through.
Lower the heat and stir in the sour cream with 2 tbsp water. Warm gently without boiling.
Stir in the cheese until just melted, season with the salt and serve with tortillas.

batch_11_part_2.json::Italian Arancini a.title: Arancini al ragù
quick_steps: Simmer the stock and saffron in a pot over medium heat, add the rice and cook until tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Stir through the butter and Parmesan, then spread on a tray and cool completely.
With damp hands, flatten a handful of cold rice, add a teaspoon of beef ragù and a cube of mozzarella, and enclose into a compact ball.
Coat each ball in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a deep pot, less than half full, over medium-high heat to 170–175°C. Fry in small batches for 4–6 minutes until deep golden and heated through, then drain on a rack.

stages.title: Cook and chill rice
steps: Bring stock and saffron to a simmer; add rice and cook, stirring often, until tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in butter and Parmesan, spread on a tray and cool completely before shaping.

stages.title: Fill and crumb
steps: With damp hands flatten a handful of cold rice, add a teaspoon of thick beef ragù and a cube of mozzarella.
Enclose filling completely and form a compact ball; repeat, then coat each in flour, egg and breadcrumbs.

stages.title: Fry and drain
steps: Heat oil in a deep heavy pot to 170–175°C, keeping the pot less than half full.
Fry balls in small batches for 4–6 minutes until deep golden and heated through; drain on a rack and rest briefly before serving.

batch_11_part_2.json::Turkish Ezogelin S.title: Ezogelin soup
quick_steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion for about 8 minutes until soft and translucent, then add the tomato and red pepper pastes and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed lentils, bulgur and stock, then bring to a gentle boil.
Simmer for 20–25 minutes until the lentils break down and the bulgur is soft.
Stir in the dried mint and paprika, adding hot water if the soup is too thick.
Season with salt and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing.

stages.title: Soften onion
steps: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat and cook diced onion until soft and translucent.
Stir in tomato and pepper pastes and cook 1 minute to deepen flavour.

stages.title: Simmer grains
steps: Add rinsed lentils, bulgur and stock; bring to a gentle boil.
Simmer 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils break down and bulgur softens.

stages.title: Season and serve
steps: Stir in dried mint and paprika, thinning with hot water if needed.
Season with salt and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing.

batch_11_part_2.json::Filipino Ginataang.title: Ginataang kalabasa
quick_steps: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until translucent, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the fish sauce and 100 ml water.
Add the pumpkin, cover and simmer for 10 minutes until nearly tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring back to a gentle simmer.
Add the green beans and cook for 5–8 minutes until just tender.
Season to taste and serve with rice, if using.

stages.title: Soften aromatics
steps: Cook onion in oil over medium heat until translucent, then add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in fish sauce and 100 ml water.

stages.title: Cook pumpkin
steps: Add pumpkin and simmer covered for 10 minutes until nearly tender.
Pour in coconut milk and bring back to a gentle simmer.

stages.title: Finish beans
steps: Add green beans and cook 5–8 minutes until just tender.
Season to taste and serve with rice.

batch_11_part_2.json::Ethiopian Shiro Wa.title: Shiro wat
quick_steps: Soften the onion in the oil in a pan over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, until sweet.
Add the garlic, berbere and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk the chickpea flour into 250 ml of the cold water until completely smooth, then slowly pour it into the pan.
Add the remaining water gradually and simmer over low heat for 15–20 minutes, until thick and silky.
Season with salt and serve with flatbread, if you like.

batch_11_part_2.json::Greek Kolokithokef.title: Kolokithokeftedes
quick_steps: Grate the courgettes, toss with salt and rest for 10 minutes, then squeeze out as much water as possible in a clean towel.
Mix the courgettes with the crumbled feta, eggs, flour, chopped dill, mint and spring onions until the mixture just holds together.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat and spoon in small patties.
Cook 3–4 minutes each side until golden and cooked through, then drain on a rack.

batch_11_part_2.json::French Far Breton.title: Far breton
quick_steps: Heat the oven to 180°C. Butter a 24 cm baking dish and scatter the prunes evenly over the base.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then add the flour until smooth.
Gradually whisk in the milk and vanilla to make a thin custard batter.
Pour the batter over the prunes and bake for 40–45 minutes, until puffed and golden with a slight wobble.
Cool until set, then slice.

batch_11_part_2.json::Korean Dubu Jorim.title: Dubu jorim
quick_steps: Drain the tofu, pat dry and slice into thick rectangles. Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat.
Cook the tofu 3–4 minutes per side until golden and lightly crisp.
Whisk the soy sauce, gochugaru, garlic, sugar and water together.
Pour the sauce around the tofu and simmer 5–7 minutes until slightly reduced.
Spoon the glaze over the tofu and finish with the spring onions and sesame oil.

batch_11_part_2.json::Japanese Kabocha N.title: Kabocha nimono
quick_steps: Remove the kabocha seeds and cut into even chunks, leaving some skin on. Place skin-side down in a snug saucepan.
Stir the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar together until the sugar dissolves. Pour over the pumpkin so it is partly submerged.
Cover with a parchment or loose lid and simmer over low heat for 15–20 minutes, until a skewer slides in easily.
Rest the pumpkin in the broth for 5 minutes, then serve.

batch_11_part_2.json::Mexican Enfrijolad.title: Enfrijoladas
quick_steps: Blend the black beans with the stock, garlic, half the onion and the chipotle until smooth. Add a little more stock if needed to make a pourable sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat. Simmer the blended beans for 8–10 minutes until silky, then season.
Keep the sauce warm over low heat.
Warm the tortillas in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat until flexible.
Dip each tortilla in the sauce and fold onto plates. Top with crumbled queso fresco, the remaining onion and coriander.

batch_11_part_2.json::Algerian Hmiss.title: Hmiss
quick_steps: Grill the whole capsicums and tomatoes, turning, until the skins blister and the flesh softens, about 20 minutes.
Cover briefly, then peel the capsicums, remove the seeds and chop them with the tomatoes.
Warm the olive oil in a pan over low heat and cook the minced garlic for 30 seconds. Add the cumin and cook until fragrant, without browning.
Add the chopped capsicums and tomatoes and cook until the excess moisture evaporates, about 15 minutes.
Mash coarsely, season with the salt and lemon juice, and serve with bread.
